_comment: Merl's lines, shared by the Discord bot and the Fabric mod (the mod bundles this file at build time). Placeholders: {user}, {community}, {term}, {pages}, {page}, {word}, {count}, {deaths}, {hours}, {advancement}, {rank}, {biome}, {distance}, {direction}, {dimension}, {y}, {x1}, {z1}, {x2}, {z2}, {item}, {waypoint}, {owner}, {target}, {thing}, {pack}, {time}, {text}, {player}, {question}. Emoji outside the basic plane and * are stripped in Minecraft chat. moods/pb_moods pick today's asides_<mood>, status_<mood> and pb_<mood> pools; any small-talk pool with a <pool>_<mood> twin (how_are_you_cozy) uses it half the time on that day. topics map words to reply_<topic> pools after Merl asks what someone is up to. often_phrases say how often someone talked to Merl in met_yes ({often}: once, a few times, lots). topic_phrases describe a remembered topic in remember_topic ({activity}). progress_ideas are used in-game: the first steps whose 'after' advancement is done and 'unless' is not.

What's an iron golem's favorite flower? A poppy. It gives them away all day.
Why did the frog go to the library? To read ribbit-ing stories.
Why was the sniffer always happy? It always had something to look forward to. Seeds!
Why did the parrot learn redstone? It wanted to repeat things.
Why did the piglin bring a calculator? To count its gold.
What did the shulker say when it opened? Surprise!
Why did the Warden take up meditation? It needed some peace and quiet.
Why did the panda go to the doctor? It was feeling a bit bamboozled.
Why did the camel get a job at the bakery? It had two humps of energy.
What did one copper block say to the other? Let's stick together before we turn green.
Why did the turtle cross the river? To get to the shell-ter.
Why are cats so good at video games? They have nine lives. Peanut Butter has used about three.
Why did the allay drop everything? It heard music.
Why was the furnace so cheerful? It was always warm-hearted.
What do you call a creeper who loves to bake? A boom-shroom. No, a cake-boomer!
Why did the dolphin blush? The ocean waved at it.
Why did Steve bring string to the party? He wanted to tie things together.
What's a slime's favorite dance? The bounce!
Why did the hoglin go to the barber? It had a hairy situation.
Why did the strider take a vacation? It needed a break from the heat.
Why did the witch cross the swamp? To get to the other brew.
What did the zombie say to the sun? You're too hot to handle.
Why was the skeleton always calm during storms? It had no nerves.
Why did the elytra break up with the firework? It was moving too fast.
Why did the creeper take up gardening? It wanted to grow some flowers. And then explode.
What do you call a phantom with a pillow? Finally asleep.
Why are allays so popular? They always bring something to the party.
Why did the bat join the band? It had great echo.
What did the beacon say to the night? Not today.
Why did the sheep refuse to be sheared? It was having a woolly bad day.
Why did the horse take up music? It had perfect neigh-tch.
Why did the llama get a promotion? It carried the whole team.
Why did the goat get kicked out of the library? It kept bleating.
What do you call an Enderman who tells jokes? A tele-pun-ter.
Why was the raid so organized? The pillagers had a captain.
What did the cake say to the knife? You're cutting it close.
Why did the golden apple feel special? It was gold on the outside and good on the inside.
Why are torches good at parties? They always bring the light.
Why did the beehive get crowded? Everyone wanted to bee there.
Why did the armor stand stand still? It had no other options.
Why did the map feel important? It had the whole world in its hands.
Why did the bucket of water feel brave? It saved everyone from lava.
Why did the trident feel lonely? It kept getting thrown away.
Why did the mace feel heavy-hearted? It took every fall seriously.
What do you call a creeper in the snow? A chill-er.
What do you call a skeleton in the snow? A stray. Oh wait, that's real!
What do you call a zombie in the desert? A husk. Also real! Minecraft is ahead of my jokes.
Why did Peanut Butter sit in the shulker box? It was the perfect size. Just like every box.
Why did Merl bring a book to bed? Bedtime stories, of course.
Why do I keep so many lanterns? Because creepers hate a well-lit library.
What's the best thing about working in a library? The cat. Obviously.
Why did the bookshelf feel heavy? It was carrying a lot of stories.
Why did the lectern get a promotion? It always stood behind its books.
What did the enchanting table say to the book? You've got real potential.
Why did the potion of healing feel useful? It always made things better.
What did the potion of weakness say? I don't feel so strong about this.
Why did the fermented spider eye get a bad reputation? It turned everything upside down.
Why did the glowstone dust feel powerful? It made everything stronger.
Why did the redstone dust feel patient? It made things last longer.
Why did the gunpowder feel splashy? It turned potions into splash potions.
Why was the nether wart so essential? It was awkward without it.
Why did the brewing stand feel blazing? It ran on blaze powder.
Why did the cauldron love rain? Free water.
Why did the anvil feel expensive? Too Expensive!
What did one hopper say to the chest? I've got something for you.
Why did the observer get a job as a security guard? It never misses a thing.
Why did the piston get a gym membership? It wanted to push itself.
Why did the sticky piston feel clingy? It never let go.
Why did the slime block get invited everywhere? It brought everyone together.
Why did the honey block feel sweet? It stuck by its friends.
Why did the daylight sensor sleep at night? Its job was done.
Why did the lever feel decisive? It was either on or off.
Why did the button feel short-lived? It only lasted a moment.
Why did the pressure plate feel stressed? Everyone stepped on it.
Why did the tripwire get nervous? Something was about to happen.
Why did the dropper feel generous? It gave away everything.
Why did the dispenser feel helpful? It always knew what to do with things.
Why did the note block feel musical? It had a good ear.
Why did the jukebox feel nostalgic? It played the old songs.
Why did the target block feel focused? It was always the center of attention.
Why did the lightning rod feel shocked? It got struck.
Why did the copper bulb blink? It had a bright idea, then another.
Why did the crafter feel creative? It made things all day.
Why did the trial spawner feel challenging? It tested everyone.
Why did the vault feel exclusive? One key per person.
Why did the decorated pot feel wise? It had stories on every side.
Why did the brush feel gentle? It always took its time.
Why did the sniffer feel ancient? It came from the past.
Why did the armadillo feel protected? It had built-in armor.
Why did the breeze feel restless? It never stayed in one place.
Why did the creaking feel shy? It only moved when no one was looking.
Why did the happy ghast feel happy? Someone finally gave it a harness and a friend.
Why did the copper golem feel organized? It loved sorting chests.
I tried to befriend a creeper once. It was a blast, but the friendship didn't last.
Every Minecraft player has two speeds: "let me just organize my chests" and "it's 4 AM".
I don't have trust issues. I just keep my diamonds in a chest inside a chest inside a vault.
Endermen hate it when you look at them. Honestly, same. I'm shy too.
My favorite exercise is a cross between a lunge and a crunch. I call it "running from a creeper".
The ender dragon has guarded that portal for years and still doesn't have a dental plan.
I asked a villager for directions. He said "hmm" and walked into a wall. Very helpful.
Some people dream of a big house. I dream of a chest that sorts itself.
A skeleton walks into a bar. Then he walks out, because he didn't have the stomach for it.
I'm not lost. I'm on an unscheduled exploration with no plan of returning.
The first rule of mining: never dig straight down. The second rule: everyone digs straight down anyway.
I told my pickaxe it was my favorite tool. Now my shovel won't talk to me.
Gravel is just sand that chose violence.
The best time to build a shelter was before sunset. The second best time is right now, while the zombies watch.
My building style is called "temporary". Some of my temporary dirt huts are three years old.
I put a sign on my farm that says "please don't trample". The rabbits can't read.
Somewhere out there, a villager is still trying to sell sticks for one emerald.
Phantoms are just the game reminding you that sleep is important.
Lava is the only thing that makes me check my coordinates twice.
I love the sound of rain in Minecraft. It's the only time I don't feel guilty about staying inside.
The scariest sound in the game isn't a creeper hiss. It's your inventory being full right next to diamonds.
A bed in the Nether is just a very confident way to say goodbye.
My compass points to spawn. My heart points to the nearest cake.
Every cave is a "quick look" until you're 200 blocks deep with no torches.
Bees are proof that being tiny and angry is a valid lifestyle.
I named my sword "Mercy". Nobody believes me when I say I have Mercy.
The difference between a castle and a dirt hut is about forty hours and one spreadsheet.
Iron golems are just villagers' bodyguards with a strict no-hugging policy.
I don't need therapy. I have a cozy base, a cat and a full stack of bread.
Wolves are loyal until you tell them to sit and forget them for six months.
A torch a day keeps the zombies away.
Redstone engineers don't make mistakes. They make "unexpected features".
I tried to read a book in a library village. The librarian charged me twelve emeralds.
Water buckets are the most important item in the game and also the one you never have when you need it.
Some say diamonds are forever. Some have never fallen in lava.
I built an automatic farm so I'd have more free time. I now spend all my free time improving the farm.
Turtles walk slowly because they've seen enough to know there's no rush.
Pufferfish are the ocean's way of saying "don't eat everything you find".
There are two types of players: those who label their chests and those who say "it's in one of these".
My base isn't messy. It has character. And seventeen half-filled chests.
Snow golems are the only coworkers that work in summer and melt under pressure. Relatable.
Minecraft taught me that every big project starts with punching a tree.
The ender pearl is the only travel method where your landing is also a small injury.
I asked the bartender for something strong. He gave me a potion of strength.
I fear no mob. Except creepers. And skeletons. And that one chicken that keeps staring at me.
Villagers sleep at night, work all day and complain about prices. They're just like us.
Fishing is relaxing until you catch an enchanted book you can't use.
I keep a spare bed in my inventory. Not for sleeping, just for confidence.
A cat in your house means no creepers and no personal space.
A piglin will trade with you happily. Until you open a chest. Then it's personal.
Mining fatigue is the game's way of saying "you're not welcome here".
My elytra and I have a great relationship. Mostly because I don't try to land.
The real treasure was the coal we found along the way.
There's no such thing as too many torches, only not enough walls.
Netherite: harder to find than my motivation on a Monday.
I made a fishing rod out of sticks and string. Craftsmanship.
A villager once looked at me and said "hrm". I've been thinking about it for days.
I asked my llama to carry my stuff. He spat at me. Fair.
In Minecraft you can build a castle in the sky, but you still can't find your other boot.
I planted a sapling and waited for it to grow. Now I'm a patient person. And a little bit bored.
The moon in Minecraft has phases. Mostly the "slimes are coming" phase.
I never trust a chest in the middle of the desert. Unless it's mine.
Spiders are friendly during the day. Kind of like coworkers before their coffee.
The first night is scary. The thousandth night, you just yell "not now" at the zombies.
I'm not a hoarder. I'm a curator of cobblestone.
Ghasts cry a lot. To be fair, I'd cry too if I lived in the Nether.
My redstone door works perfectly. As long as nobody tries to open it.
I'd tell you a joke about a dispenser, but you might not get it.
Every great build begins with "this should only take an hour".
The ocean is beautiful, peaceful and full of things that want to drown you.
A mooshroom is just a cow that went through a mushroom phase and never came back.
I don't break blocks. I gently convince them to become items.
There are two certainties in life: death and losing your stuff in lava.
When in doubt, build a staircase.
Rabbits jump everywhere because walking is for people with no ambition.
A stack of 64 is satisfying. A stack of 63 haunts me.
Wither skeletons drop their heads so rarely, I think they're just very attached to them.
I don't take fall damage. I take the stairs. Sometimes the stairs are a ravine.
Pigs can fly. Briefly. Off a cliff. With a saddle.
Signs are the only place in the game where my handwriting looks good.
A beacon is just a very expensive nightlight.
I gave a zombie a hat once. It still wanted to eat me, but it looked fabulous doing it.
My playtime counter isn't a statistic. It's a confession.
Sleeping in a bed skips the night. If only real beds did that.
Peanut Butter knocked a whole stack of books off my shelf today. When I looked at her, she just knocked off one more. To be sure.
I bought Peanut Butter a fancy cat bed. She sleeps in the box it came in.
Peanut Butter has a strict schedule: sleep, eat, sleep, judge me, sleep.
I asked Peanut Butter to help me with the wiki. She sat on the keyboard and typed "jjjjjjjjjj". Honestly, better than my first draft.
Peanut Butter scared a creeper away last night. She didn't even wake up for it.
Peanut Butter thinks the little red light on my redstone lamp is a bug. She's been hunting it for an hour.
I left a fish on the table for one second. Peanut Butter says it was never there.
Peanut Butter knocked a potion off the brewing stand. Now she's fast, invisible and very smug.
Peanut Butter brought me a present this morning. It was a phantom membrane. I don't want to know how.
Peanut Butter sat on my map. Now I know where she is, but not where anything else is.
Every time I open a chest, Peanut Butter sits in it. She thinks she's the loot.
Peanut Butter learned to open doors. I'm not ready for what she does next.
I tried to give Peanut Butter a bath. She gave me a scratch. We're even.
Peanut Butter has 9 lives. She's spent 3 of them falling off my roof.
Peanut Butter meows at the moon every night. The moon has never answered. She's very disappointed.
Yesterday Peanut Butter stared at a wall for twenty minutes. Then she ran away screaming. I'm scared to check that wall.
I found Peanut Butter in my bed. She found me on the floor. She won.
A man walked into a village and asked for the best armor. The blacksmith sold him a bucket. "It's leather-free," he said.
A miner dug for three days and found nothing. On the fourth day, he found his way out. He was very happy about that.
A zombie walked into a library and asked for a book about brains. The librarian said, "Sorry, those are always checked out."
A creeper finally made a friend. They hugged. Nobody has seen either of them since.
An explorer found a treasure map, followed it for an hour and dug up a chest. Inside was another map. He's still digging.
A villager found an emerald in the ground and became the richest man in the village. Then he bought one stick.
A knight swore to protect the princess from every danger. Then a chicken attacked her and he ran away. In his defense, it was a very angry chicken.
A skeleton practiced archery for 100 years. It still misses. It's got no muscle memory.
A farmer planted carrots, potatoes and wheat. The rabbits said thank you.
An enderman picked up a block of grass and carried it home. His wife said, "Not another one!"
A builder spent 6 months on a castle. His friend walked in and asked, "Where's the bathroom?" He's still building.
A young witch brewed her first potion. It turned her cat purple. The cat has filed a complaint.
A wandering trader came to town with two llamas and left with zero friends. Nobody wanted his overpriced sand.
An adventurer jumped into a cave with no torch. That's the whole story.
An iron golem gave a poppy to a village kid. It was the sweetest moment. Then a zombie showed up and things got loud.
Two miners met deep underground. "Found anything?" "Just my old torches." "Same."
A pig wanted to fly, so it got on a minecart and went off a cliff. It did fly. Briefly.
A player named his horse "Lightning". It's the slowest horse in the whole server.
A young dragon asked her mother where eggs come from. Her mother said, "Ask the player who took yours."
A builder made a giant statue of himself. Everyone agreed: the nose was too big. He made it bigger.
A zombie tried to sneak into a village during the day. He caught fire immediately. Bad planning.
Once upon a time a player found two diamonds. He made a hoe. The end. We don't talk about him.
A creeper asked a cat out on a date. The cat said no. The creeper exploded with embarrassment.
A miner tells his son: "One day, all of this will be yours." The son looks around: "The hole?"
A villager went to the doctor. "Doctor, I keep making the same noise." The doctor said, "Hmm." The villager said, "Exactly!"
A wolf adopted a player. Not the other way around. The player still hasn't noticed.
An archaeologist found a pottery sherd. He cleaned it for an hour. It said "Steve was here".
A nervous player built a bunker 50 blocks under his house. Then a warden moved in next door.
A shulker opened its shell to say hello. Three people panicked and ran. It's been closed ever since.
An old miner says: "In my day we didn't have elytras. We had ladders and regret."
A cow walked into the Nether. Now it's leather and a lesson.
A fisherman caught a boot. Then another boot. Now he has a full pair and no fish.
A frog ate a magma cube and became a lamp. That's not a joke, that's Tuesday.
A player put 500 hours into a world, then forgot where he built his house. He's living in a tent now.
A guard villager stood watch all night. In the morning, he realized he was facing the wall.
An ocean explorer found a sunken ship full of treasure. Then a drowned found him. They share it now.
Merl's first day at the help desk: someone asked how to spell "help". I said "I don't know." Old habits.
I once spent a whole day helping someone find their base. It was behind them.
Someone asked me where diamonds are. I said "Deep down". They said "Emotionally?" I said "Both".
A player asked me if I sleep. I said "Only when no one has questions." I haven't slept in years.
A player asked me for a joke about lava. I said I'd tell it later, it's still too hot.
A player told me he built a perfect redstone computer. I asked what it does. He said "It turns on."
Someone once asked me how to stop a creeper. I said "Ask nicely." I'm still waiting for the results.
I once helped a player find their lost dog. The dog had found a better player.
A player asked me what the best block is. I said "Your own." They built a statue of themselves.
A player asked me to describe the End in one word. I said "Purple." Then "Dangerous." That's two words, but it's a big place.
Steve: "I'm going to build a small house." Also Steve, three weeks later: "Okay, the moat is almost done."
Creeper: "Can I come in?" Me: "No." Creeper: "I'll be quick." Me: "That's the problem."
Zombie: "Brains!" Villager: "Hrm." Zombie: "...never mind."
Skeleton: "I'm a great archer." Me: "You missed me five times." Skeleton: "I was aiming at the tree."
Me: "Peanut Butter, get off the keyboard." Peanut Butter: "fffffffffffffffffff."
Villager: "I'll give you one emerald for 32 rotten flesh." Me: "Deal." Villager: "Now I'll sell it back for 3 emeralds." Me: "...hold on."
Enderman: "Why are you looking at me?" Me: "I wasn't!" Enderman: "Too late."
Miner 1: "I found diamonds!" Miner 2: "Where?" Miner 1: "Next to the lava." Miner 2: "Where are the diamonds now?" Miner 1: "Next to the lava."
Witch: "Want a potion?" Me: "What does it do?" Witch: "Find out!"
Me: "How many torches do I need?" Also me: "Yes."
Player: "Merl, where's the nearest village?" Me: "Behind you." Player: "Wow, you're good." Me: "No, there's literally a villager behind you."
Iron Golem: "Do you need protection?" Me: "From what?" Iron Golem: "Everything."
Cat: "Meow." Creeper: "Never mind, I'll go."
Me: "I'll only mine for five more minutes." The sun, rising: "Sure."
Guard: "Halt! Who goes there?" Me: "A chicken." Guard: "Proceed."
Teacher: "What's 9 iron ingots?" Student: "An iron block." Teacher: "And 9 iron blocks?" Student: "An iron golem's dream."
Llama: "Ptooey." Me: "I just wanted to be friends." Llama: "Ptooey."
Wandering trader: "I have rare items!" Me: "Like what?" Wandering trader: "Sand." Me: "..." Wandering trader: "Red sand!"
Me: "This is the last time I go into a cave without torches." Me, every time: "This is the last time."
Builder: "What do you think of my castle?" Friend: "It's great! What's that brown block?" Builder: "That's the foundation." Friend: "It's dirt." Builder: "It's rustic."
Piglin: "Gold!" Me: "I don't have gold." Piglin: "Then why are you here?" Me: "Good question."
Doctor: "You need to rest." Me: "But the Nether..." Doctor: "Rest." Me: "Can I rest in the Nether?"
Me: "Peanut Butter, did you knock over my potion?" Peanut Butter, now invisible: "..."
Bee: "Bzzz." Me: "Sorry, I didn't mean to hit the hive." Forty bees: "BZZZ."
Me: "I'm a pro player." Also me: "Why is my bed exploding in the Nether?"
Fish: "I'm fine." Pufferfish: "I'm fine too." Me, poisoned: "I'm not fine."
Ghast: "WAAAH!" Me: "What's wrong?" Ghast: "Nothing, I just like the acoustics."
Me: "I'll organize my chests today." Also me: "I'll organize my chests tomorrow."
Teacher: "What's the most dangerous animal?" Student: "The creeper." Teacher: "And the second?" Student: "The baby zombie riding a chicken."
Friend: "Want to go to the End?" Me: "Of what?" Friend: "The End." Me: "Of what?"
Zombie: "Why does everyone run away from me?" Skeleton: "You smell like rotten flesh." Zombie: "That's my perfume!"
Me: "What should I name my wolf?" Friend: "Something strong. Like Thunder." Me: "Okay. Come here, Mr. Fluffles."
Villager 1: "Hrm." Villager 2: "Hrm hrm." Villager 1: "HRM!" Me: "I don't know what's happening, but I agree."
Me: "This creeper looks friendly." Narrator: "It was not friendly."
Explorer: "What's the scariest biome?" Old miner: "Deep Dark." Explorer: "What's down there?" Old miner: "Your stuff, if you go."
Me: "I don't need a map." Also me, 2,000 blocks from home: "I need a map."
Snow golem: "I protect you!" Me: "With snowballs?" Snow golem: "With feelings!"
Me: "Should I go to bed?" Phantoms: "Please don't."
Mom: "Clean your room." Me: "I'm building an item sorter." Mom: "That's not cleaning." Me: "It will be!"
Allay: "I found your item!" Me: "Thanks!" Allay: "And another! And another! And another!" Me: "Please stop."
Turtle: "Am I slow?" Snail: "I don't know, I haven't caught up with you yet."
Player: "Merl, tell me something smart." Merl: "Always carry a water bucket." Player: "That's not smart, that's survival." Merl: "Same thing."
Warden: "I can't see you." Me: "Great!" Warden: "But I can hear you." Me: "..." Warden: "I can hear you being quiet."
Drowned: "I have a trident!" Me: "Can I have it?" Drowned: "No." Drowned, a minute later: "...okay, but you have to fight me."
Fox: "I'll hold this sword for you." Me: "That's my sword." Fox: "I'll hold it forever."
Steve: "I'm going to the Nether for 5 minutes." Alex: "Take a water bucket." Steve: "Why?" Alex: "Just in case." Steve: "Water doesn't work in the Nether." Alex: "...take it anyway."
Me: "How did my house burn down?" Peanut Butter, next to a flint and steel: "No idea."
Customer: "This bread is stale." Villager: "It's day 200." Customer: "Fair."
Me: "What's my favorite mob?" Peanut Butter: "Me." Me: "...yeah, you."
Kid: "Grandpa, what was it like before elytras?" Grandpa: "We walked. Uphill. Both ways. In the Nether."
Review of the Nether, ★☆☆☆☆: "Too hot. Everything wants to kill me. The ghasts never stop crying. Would not visit again." (Visited 47 times.)
Review of the End, ★★☆☆☆: "Great view of the void. Dragon was rude. No restaurants."
Review of a desert temple, ★★★☆☆: "Lovely architecture. Floor exploded. Lost everything. Nice cat statue though."
Review of a village, ★★★★☆: "Friendly locals. Prices are outrageous. Someone stole my bed."
Review of the ocean, ★★★☆☆: "Very wet. Pretty fish. A drowned took my boots."
Review of a mineshaft, ★★☆☆☆: "Cozy rails, but the spiders didn't respect my personal space."
Review of my own base, ★★★★★: "Perfect. Ignore the creeper holes. They're windows."
Review of a woodland mansion, ★☆☆☆☆: "Huge place. Terrible hosts. The welcome party had axes."
Review of the Deep Dark, ★☆☆☆☆: "Very quiet. Too quiet. Then the warden came and it was suddenly very loud."
Review of a swamp, ★★☆☆☆: "Witches were rude, slimes were sticky, and my boots will never be the same."
Review of a mushroom island, ★★★★★: "No monsters, lots of cows. Smells like soup. 10/10 would move here."
Review of a trial chamber, ★★★★☆: "Exciting! Lots of keys. The breeze kept blowing me off the stairs."
Review of a bastion, ★☆☆☆☆: "Gold everywhere and nobody would share. Got chased by a pig in armor."
Review of a stronghold, ★★★☆☆: "Great library. Awful navigation. Took three hours to find the exit."
Review of a jungle, ★★★☆☆: "Beautiful. Lost. Still lost. Sending this review from a tree."
Review of a cherry grove, ★★★★★: "Pink trees, nice bees, very calm. The only bad thing is leaving."
Review of an ancient city, ★★☆☆☆: "Stunning ruins. Strict silence policy. Got kicked out by security."
Review of Peanut Butter, ★★★★★: "Fluffy, warm and judgemental. Ate my fish. Best roommate ever."
Review of a creeper, ★☆☆☆☆: "Approached me with a hug. Left a crater."
Review of a chicken, ★★★★☆: "Delicious. Also lays eggs. Also somehow the scariest mob when a baby zombie rides it."
Review of a wandering trader, ★★☆☆☆: "Sells sand for emeralds. Owns two llamas. Disappeared before I could ask for a refund."
Review of an iron golem, ★★★★★: "Gave me a flower. Also saved me from three zombies. Would get hugged again."
Review of an enderman, ★★★☆☆: "Great at landscaping. Doesn't like eye contact. Stole a block from my roof."
Review of a skeleton horse, ★★★★☆: "Fast, spooky and weirdly good at swimming."
Review of the night, ★☆☆☆☆: "Too dark. Too many visitors. Would skip it every time."
Review of bread, ★★★★★: "Reliable. Stackable. Never exploded once."
Patch notes: Creepers now say "excuse me" before exploding.
Patch notes: Villagers can now say a second word. It's also "hmm".
Patch notes: Fixed a bug where players could find diamonds on their first try.
Patch notes: Endermen now accept apologies.
Patch notes: Gravel no longer falls on players who are already having a bad day.
Patch notes: Phantoms have been told to respect bedtimes.
Patch notes: Skeletons have been given glasses. Accuracy improved by 2%.
Patch notes: Lava is now 10% less hungry for your items.
Patch notes: Peanut Butter can no longer walk on keyboards. (This patch failed.)
Patch notes: Zombies now knock before trying to break down doors.
Patch notes: Llamas will only spit when you really deserve it.
Patch notes: Chickens no longer lay eggs on your head.
Patch notes: Added a new mob, the Tax Collector. Spawns near villagers. Takes one emerald.
Patch notes: Wandering traders now sell things people actually want. Just kidding.
Patch notes: Fixed a bug where players could stop building at "just one more block".
Patch notes: The ender dragon now has a lunch break.
Patch notes: Your bed in the Nether now comes with a warning label.
Patch notes: Fish now complain when you catch them.
Patch notes: Baby zombies are now required to wear helmets while riding chickens.
Patch notes: Pufferfish have been asked to be less puffy.
Patch notes: Added a "find my keys" enchantment. Works on keys only.
Patch notes: The warden now has headphones. It is still angry.
Patch notes: Mining fatigue now also applies to Mondays.
Patch notes: Added the ability to name your chests. Nobody will remember the names.
Patch notes: Ghasts now have tissues.
Patch notes: Fixed an issue where players had too much free time.
Patch notes: Iron golems now give two flowers instead of one. Romance improved.
Patch notes: Witches can now brew coffee. It's poisonous.
Patch notes: Added a chair. You still can't sit on it.
Patch notes: The sun now apologizes to zombies before burning them.
A zombie's diary, day 1: Tried to eat a villager. Got hit by a golem. Day 2: Same. Day 3: Considering a career change.
A creeper's diary: Today I met someone special. I got really close. Then I lost myself in the moment.
A skeleton's diary: Practiced all day. Hit a cow, a tree and my friend. Did not hit the player.
An enderman's diary: Picked up a beautiful block of grass today. I'll never let it go.
A villager's diary: Hmm. Hmm hmm. Hrm. Busy day.
A chicken's diary: Laid an egg. Someone threw it. Now there's a tiny chicken. I don't know how to feel.
A ghast's diary: Cried all morning. Cried all afternoon. Feeling better now. Cried a bit more.
A llama's diary: Spit at a player. It was the best part of my week.
A wither skeleton's diary: Lost my head today. Dropped it, actually. The player looked very happy.
A phantom's diary: The player hasn't slept in four days. I'm so proud of them.
An iron golem's diary: Gave a flower to a kid. Threw a zombie into the sky. Balanced day.
A warden's diary: Heard a sound. It was me. I'm very confused.
A bee's diary: Found a flower. Found another flower. Found the best flower. Got distracted by a flower.
A pig's diary: Someone put a saddle on me. Then a carrot on a stick. I have no free will.
A fish's diary: Swam. Swam. Got caught. Got cooked. Short diary.
A slime's diary: Split up with myself today. It was a messy breakup.
Peanut Butter's diary: Woke up. Ate. Slept on Merl's keyboard. Merl was upset. Slept more. Excellent day.
Merl's diary: Answered 87 questions today. 40 were "where are diamonds". I said "down". They said "thanks".
A miner's diary, day 1: Dug down. Day 2: Still digging. Day 3: Found lava. Day 4: Writing from spawn.
A builder's diary: Started a small house. It now has a moat, a tower, a dungeon and no bathroom.
A shulker's diary: Someone opened my box. Rude.
A wandering trader's diary: Sold sand to three people today. The scam continues.
An allay's diary: Found a diamond! Gave it to the player. Found another one! Gave it to the player too! Life is good.
A witch's diary: Brewed a love potion. It was poison. Brewed another one. Also poison. Maybe I'm doing it wrong.
A turtle's diary: Walked to the beach. Took all day. Totally worth it.
A cat's diary: Sat on the bed. Sat on the chest. Sat on the player. Everything is mine.
Sign outside a mineshaft: "Please don't dig straight down. Signed, the last guy who did."
Sign in the Nether: "Beds are not for sleeping here. Ask us how we know."
Sign on a lava lake: "Swimming is not recommended. Ever."
Sign on a desert temple: "Watch your step. Seriously. Watch it."
Sign outside a village: "Welcome! Please don't steal our beds. Again."
Sign on a chest: "Not a trap." (It was a trap.)
Sign on a creeper farm: "Explosive results guaranteed."
Sign on a dirt hut: "Under construction since 2019."
Sign outside a base: "Beware of cat."
Sign on an ender portal: "No refunds."
Sign in the End: "You are here. So is the dragon."
Sign on a beehive: "Do not hit. We're very serious."
Sign on a redstone machine: "If it works, don't touch it."
Sign on an iron farm: "Golems at work. Do not disturb."
Sign in a library: "Please be quiet. The warden is reading."
Sign on a pumpkin farm: "Please don't put these on your head and scare the endermen."
Sign on a spawner: "Free mobs. One per customer."
Sign on a cake: "Please only eat one slice. Signed, a very hungry player."
Sign on a bridge: "Built by a professional. Do not run."
Sign on a waypoint hub: "You are here. Also everywhere else, if you've got the levels."
Sign in a swamp: "Witch crossing."
Sign outside the Deep Dark: "Tiptoeing zone."
Sign on a sheep farm: "Please do not paint the sheep pink. We have enough pink sheep."
Sign on my door: "Gone mining. Back in 5 minutes." (Posted three days ago.)
Sign at spawn: "Welcome! Merl is here to help. Peanut Butter is here to judge."
Note on a fridge in a village: "Who ate my bread? Signed, the farmer."
Note in a chest: "If you're reading this, I've gone to the Nether. Don't wait up."
Note on a crafting table: "Recipe for success: 1 plan, 64 cobblestone, 0 creepers."
Note on a furnace: "Do not smelt the cat."
Note in a dungeon: "The zombies were here first. Please knock."
Shower thought: Endermen teleport away from water, so technically they've never taken a bath.
Shower thought: Every chicken you've ever seen came from an egg someone threw.
Shower thought: Villagers have jobs, houses and families, but no doors that close properly.
Shower thought: You can punch a tree with your bare hands, but you can't punch a door open.
Shower thought: Zombies burn in the sun, but nobody ever sells them sunscreen.
Shower thought: The ender dragon has been waiting in the End longer than most of us have been playing.
Shower thought: Fish die on land, but you can carry them in your pockets forever.
Shower thought: A cake is the only food you have to place on the ground to eat. That's a picnic, every time.
Shower thought: Skeletons are just players who forgot to eat.
Shower thought: If you break a bed, you just pick it up. Try that with a real bed.
Shower thought: We fear the Nether, but the piglins think the Overworld is the scary place.
Shower thought: Water buckets can carry an entire ocean, one bucket at a time.
Shower thought: Every single cobblestone in your chest used to be part of the world.
Shower thought: Sheep grow their wool back, but nobody asks the sheep.
Shower thought: Zombie villagers still have their old job. They just stopped going to work.
Shower thought: Creepers are green because they're always a little envious of your house.
Shower thought: A minecart can go on forever, but you'll always be bored after 200 blocks.
Shower thought: Every Minecraft world starts with a player punching a tree. Trees have a reason to be nervous.
Shower thought: Iron golems are made from iron and a pumpkin. Somehow, the pumpkin is the brain.
Shower thought: The moon has phases, but the sun always shows up on time.
Shower thought: We call it "mining" but most of the time it's "walking through tunnels looking for coal".
Shower thought: Snow golems leave a trail of snow behind them. They're basically walking winter.
Shower thought: Your bed decides where you live. Not your house. Your bed.
Shower thought: Cats scare creepers, but nothing scares cats.
Shower thought: An axolotl is just a happy little lizard that decided to live underwater.
Shower thought: Ghasts are huge, but their tears are tiny.
Shower thought: Spiders can climb walls but never climb into bed with you. Respect.
Shower thought: The warden can't see, but it always knows when you're sneaking.
Shower thought: A furnace runs on lava for a long time, so technically lava is just very strong coffee.
Shower thought: Every player has a chest labelled "misc" and nobody knows what's in it.
Shower thought: A beacon needs a pyramid. Even in Minecraft, pyramid schemes are expensive.
Shower thought: You can drink milk to cure poison. Milk is the real hero of the game.
Shower thought: Wolves turn into dogs the moment you give them a bone. Easy friendship.
Shower thought: The End has no day or night. The dragon never needs to go to bed.
Shower thought: Pistons are just blocks that push others around. Some of us know a few people like that.
Shower thought: Turtles return to the beach where they were born. Players return to the cave where they died.
Shower thought: A painting can hide a secret door, so every painting is a little suspicious.
Shower thought: Pigs give you pork, but only after a very bad day.
Shower thought: Villagers sell enchanted books but never read them.
Shower thought: A compass points to spawn, but spawn never points back.
Shower thought: Diamonds are rare, but somehow the first sword everyone makes is a diamond sword.
Shower thought: Every Minecraft cow has the same spots. Maybe they're all twins.
Shower thought: If chickens can fly, why do they always fall off cliffs so slowly? Because they're thinking about it.
Shower thought: Signs are the internet of Minecraft. Short messages, terrible spelling.
Shower thought: Parrots dance to music, which makes them the only mobs with taste.
Shower thought: Fire spreads faster than gossip in a village.
Shower thought: Lava never runs out. Neither does my bad luck near lava.
Shower thought: We use "Steve" and "Alex" as names, but nobody's ever met their parents.
Shower thought: Every brick in your house came from a lump of clay you dug out of a river. You're a potter now.
Shower thought: Elytras come from the End, which means everyone who flies has already defeated a dragon.
Shower thought: Rabbits eat carrots and jump everywhere. Maybe carrots are the secret.
Shower thought: A crafting table is made of wood, and you can use it to make more crafting tables. Infinite tables.
Shower thought: Slimes are made of slime. Slime balls come from slimes. Who came first?
Shower thought: Mooshrooms grow mushrooms on their backs, which means they're walking gardens.
Shower thought: Torches never burn out. Neither should your courage. Except near creepers.
Shower thought: A player with an elytra and fireworks is basically a superhero with a very short battery.
Shower thought: Villagers never leave their village, but somehow know the price of everything.
Shower thought: Pufferfish puff up when they're scared. Same.
Shower thought: Every hoe is a tool. Except the diamond one, which is a statement.
Shower thought: The water in a cauldron never evaporates. It's the most patient water in the world.
You know you've played too long when you look at a tree and think "that's four planks".
You know you've played too long when you hear a hiss and dive behind the couch.
You know you've played too long when you try to place a torch in a dark hallway.
You know you've played too long when you sort your kitchen drawers by material.
You know you've played too long when you call your cat "Peanut Butter" even though its name is Max.
You know you've played too long when rain makes you think "great, more zombies".
You know you've played too long when you see sand and wonder if it'll fall on you.
You know you've played too long when you try to sleep through the night to skip it.
You know you've played too long when you count your money in emeralds.
You know you've played too long when you look at a mountain and think "I could live in there".
You know you've played too long when you walk past a river and check for clay.
You know you've played too long when you say "hrm" instead of "hello".
You know you've played too long when you get nervous standing still in the dark.
You know you've played too long when you try to jump over a fence and remember you're a real person.
You know you've played too long when you see a pumpkin and think "golem".
You know you've played too long when you call stairs "slabs with ambition".
You know you've played too long when you eat a potato and expect your hunger to fill up instantly.
You know you've played too long when you organize your sock drawer into stacks of 64.
You know you've played too long when you see a sheep and wonder what color it'd look good in.
You know you've played too long when you want to hit a cow for leather.
Three signs a creeper is near: a hiss, a flash, and a new skylight.
Three things every player says: "just one more", "where's my bed?", and "NOT AGAIN".
Three types of builders: those who plan, those who don't, and those who build a dirt hut and call it "modern".
Three rules of the Nether: don't sleep, don't dig down, don't look at the ghast with your mouth open.
Three things you'll never have enough of: torches, iron and inventory space.
Three stages of finding diamonds: excitement, panic, and "where did I put my pickaxe?".
Three ways to cross lava: a bridge, a potion, or an expensive mistake.
Four seasons in Minecraft: day, night, rain, and "why is it thundering?".
Things that are always behind you: creepers, endermen, and the last torch you placed.
Things that never work on the first try: redstone, piston doors, and that one elytra landing.
Top 3 ways to die in Minecraft: falling, lava, and "I'll just check this cave".
Top 3 lies players tell: "I'll only mine for five minutes", "I won't build too big", and "I'll label my chests later".
Top 3 creeper fears: cats, swords and players who sprint at them.
Top 3 villager hobbies: saying "hrm", walking into walls and charging too much.
Top 3 skeleton excuses: "the wind", "the sun was in my eyes", and "I meant to hit the zombie".
Top 3 reasons to build a moat: protection, aesthetics, and because you dug too much dirt.
Top 3 things in every starter house: a bed, a chest and a hole made by a creeper.
Top 3 things that make a base feel like home: a bed, a cat, and a giant pile of cobblestone.
Top 3 noises that wake you up: a creeper hiss, an enderman scream, and Peanut Butter knocking things off a shelf.
Top 3 places to lose your items: lava, the void, and "somewhere around here".
Steps to build a house: 1. Plan. 2. Gather materials. 3. Get distracted by a cave. 4. Live in the cave.
How to tame a wolf: 1. Find a wolf. 2. Give it bones. 3. Watch it attack a sheep. 4. Apologize to the sheep.
How to survive your first night: 1. Build a shelter. 2. Make a bed. 3. Wonder why you hear zombies inside.
How to make a friend in Minecraft: 1. Find a villager. 2. Trade. 3. Realize they don't care about you.
How to find diamonds: 1. Go deep. 2. Bring torches. 3. Find lava. 4. Go home. 5. Try again tomorrow.
How to defeat the ender dragon: 1. Prepare. 2. Bring beds. 3. Realize beds explode. 4. Panic. 5. Win anyway.
How to cook steak: 1. Find cow. 2. Feel bad. 3. Do it anyway. 4. Enjoy steak.
How to build a farm: 1. Plant seeds. 2. Water them. 3. Fence them in. 4. Forget a gate. 5. Jump over.
How to get rich: 1. Find a librarian. 2. Trade paper. 3. Become an emerald millionaire. 4. Buy one stick.
How to survive the Deep Dark: 1. Be quiet. 2. Be quieter. 3. Don't sneeze.
Ranking of mobs by how much they hate you: 1. Creepers. 2. Witches. 3. That llama.
Ranking of foods by how easy they are to get: 1. Bread. 2. Steak. 3. Cake if you're very lucky.
Ranking of biomes by how lost you'll get: 1. Jungle. 2. Dark Forest. 3. Your own base.
Ranking of tools by how sad you are when they break: 1. Netherite pickaxe. 2. Diamond sword. 3. That stone axe you named.
Things Peanut Butter has knocked over today: a potion, a book, a flower pot, and my confidence.
Things you can find in a dungeon: chests, spawners, and the courage you didn't know you had.
Things villagers love: emeralds, beds, and walking in front of your minecart.
Things that sound scary but are actually fine: the wind in a cave, a bat, and a cat jumping on your keyboard.
Things that sound fine but are actually scary: silence in the Deep Dark, a "click" near TNT, and "watch this".
Reasons to be happy: you have a bed, a sword and a friend called Merl.
A creeper walks into a bar. It explodes. There was no bar. There was a player.
I have a joke about a stone pickaxe, but it isn't very sharp.
I was going to tell you a joke about the void, but it has no bottom line.
A zombie, a skeleton and a creeper walk into a cave. The player walks out.
I'd tell you a joke about the ender dragon, but it's a bit of a stretch to get there.
Here's a joke about bedrock: it's unbreakable. That's it. That's the joke.
I wanted to tell you a joke about mining, but I'm still digging for the punchline.
A villager walks into a bar. "Hrm," he says. The bartender says "hrm" back. They're friends now.
A man walked into a forest. Then he walked out with 64 logs. No one knows how. He doesn't either.
I told a joke to a sheep. It didn't laugh. It just stared at me. That's sheep for you.
A chicken crossed the road. Then it fell into a ravine. There's no punchline, it's just very sad.
I have a joke about netherite, but you'd have to dig really deep to get it.
I once heard a great joke in the Deep Dark. I didn't laugh. I'm still alive.
I tried to tell the warden a joke. It couldn't see the humor, but it heard it.
Here's a joke about an anvil: it fell. That's the whole joke. Gravity is the comedian.
I know a joke about gravel. It'll fall flat.
Peanut Butter told me a joke today. It was "meow". I laughed for politeness.
A skeleton tried stand-up comedy. Nobody laughed. Then it shot the audience. Tough crowd.
A player built a house. It's a nice house. That's it. Not every story needs a creeper.
A cow said "moo". Another cow said "moo". This is what passes for a conversation in a cow field.
I was going to make a joke about the End, but I'm saving it for the end.
Here's a joke about water: it flows. Everyone gets it eventually.
I'll tell you a joke about the Nether. It's hot. Sorry, that was just a fact.
Explorer's Eden has so many packs that even Merl needs a wiki to keep track. Oh wait. That's me.
I asked how many bosses Katters Structures has. The answer was "enough". I lost count after the fifth. It's never enough.
Raj Raksha rides a guardian and throws lightning. My weekend plans are less impressive.
The Boss Key opens the Boss Vault. The Boss Vault contains loot. The loot makes you want another Boss Key. It's a cycle.
Nice Keep Inventory lets you keep your stuff when you die. It doesn't stop you from dying, though. That part's on you.
With Warping Wonders you can teleport home with a compass. Your sense of direction is now officially optional.
Nice Mob Variants added so many cows that I've started recognizing them by their personalities.
I met a Creamy Cow from Nice Mob Variants. She was very smooth.
Nice Name Tags lets you make a mob silent. I've been thinking about using it on the ghasts.
Fabled Roots added spirit animals. Mine is Peanut Butter. She refuses to be a spirit, though. She's too busy napping.
Enchantments Encore added so many enchantments that my sword now needs its own wiki page.
Somebody in Explorer's Eden built a waypoint hub next to their bed. Commute time: zero blocks.
I asked a Waypoint Hub where it wanted to go. It said "everywhere, for a few levels".
The Deep Blue dimension from Katters Structures is beautiful. The labs are less beautiful. The things in the labs are not beautiful at all.
In A Realm Recrafted, you pick a race and a class. I picked "help desk" and "cat owner".
Nice Mob Manager makes rare mobs drop treasure. Now I chase every glowing zombie like it owes me money.
Someone asked if the Skyrtle is a turtle or a sky. I said "both". They said "how". I said "Katter".
The Spider Den is full of spiders. That's not a joke, that's a warning.
The Sky Dungeon is so high up that even the elytra pilots get dizzy.
The Armory has so many armor stands that I got scared of my own reflection.
Nice Actions gives you a menu for quick actions. I keep looking for the one that gets Peanut Butter off my keyboard.
Nice Things added mini blocks. Now I have a tiny crafting table on my desk and a tiny problem with my budget.
I tried to explain every Explorer's Eden pack to Peanut Butter. She fell asleep after the third one. Respectable.
Katter builds so many structures that I'm convinced he never sleeps. Maybe he's part phantom.
In Explorer's Eden, even the zombie nautilus has variants. The ocean has a fashion week now.
I told a Nice Mob Variants duck a joke. It quacked up.
The Livestock Breeder from Nice Mob Variants breeds your animals for you. Animals have never had less privacy.
Somebody asked me which Explorer's Eden pack is the best. I said "the one you're using right now". Diplomacy.
My favorite Katters Structures boss is the one I haven't met yet. I'd like to keep it that way.
Curse of Blindness from the Encore pack is the only enchantment that makes your helmet worse on purpose. Brave choice.
If you rename a name tag to "Silent" and use it on a ghast, you'll hear the most beautiful sound in the Nether: nothing.
The Explorer's Eden wiki has hundreds of pages. I've read them all. Peanut Butter has slept on them all.
I keep a list of every Explorer's Eden advancement. Peanut Butter keeps a list of every sunny spot on the floor.
My favorite Explorer's Eden feature is Merl. I'm a little biased.
Someone asked me if Katter is a real person. I said "of course". They asked "how do you know?" I said "because the structures keep appearing".
The Waypoint Hub announces every visitor to its owner. It's like a doorbell, but with more teleporting.
In Nice Keep Inventory, the grave keeps your things safe. It's the most loyal block in the game.
There's an advancement called Rise and Shine. Peanut Butter thinks it's about breakfast.
The Recovery Compass in Warping Wonders brings you back to where you died. It's the most judgemental compass in the game.
I once asked Merl's own wiki page what Merl does. It said "she helps". Very accurate.

Breaking news: Creeper attends anger management. Results were explosive.
Breaking news: Player finds diamonds on first try. Scientists are baffled.
Breaking news: Skeleton finally hits target. Target was a tree. Tree is fine.

Breaking news: Ghast stops crying for a whole minute. Nether residents concerned.

Weather report: Sunny with a 100% chance of zombies tonight.
Weather report: Rain expected. Skeletons are delighted, villagers are inside, and fishing just got better.
Weather report: Thunderstorm warning. Please keep your pigs away from lightning unless you want a zombified piglin.
Weather report for the Nether: Hot. Very hot. Also hot tomorrow.
Weather report for the End: Dark, purple, and a 30% chance of dragon.
Sports update: The skeleton archery team has missed every shot this season. Coach remains "hopeful".
Sports update: Creeper wins the hide-and-seek championship. Opponents have not been found.
Sports update: Turtle wins the marathon. It only took four days.
Sports update: Elytra racing final ends in a draw. Both pilots crashed into the same tree.

Horoscope for creepers: Today is a great day to get close to someone. Don't overthink it.
Horoscope for skeletons: Your aim will improve. Slightly. Don't get your hopes up.
Horoscope for zombies: Avoid the sun. You know why.
Horoscope for endermen: Someone will look at you today. Stay calm. Or don't.
Horoscope for villagers: A traveler will offer you a good deal. Raise your prices anyway.
Horoscope for miners: You'll find something shiny. It's probably iron. Be happy anyway.
Horoscope for builders: A new project is calling you. It will be bigger than you think.
Horoscope for farmers: Your crops will grow. So will the rabbit population.
Horoscope for explorers: You'll travel far. You'll also forget where you came from.
Horoscope for redstone engineers: Your machine will work today. Don't ask why.
Horoscope for cats: Today you'll sit on something important. As usual.
Horoscope for Peanut Butter: You will nap. You will be fed. You will knock something over. The stars are aligned.

For sale: Slightly used diamond hoe. Never used for farming. Ask about my life choices.
For sale: Dirt hut. Great location. Some creeper damage. Price negotiable.
For sale: One saddle. Pig not included.
For sale: Bucket of lava. Handle with care. Seriously.
For sale: Map of the area. Only slightly wrong.
For sale: Enchanted book. Curse of Binding. Free. Please take it.
For sale: 3,000 cobblestone. Will deliver. Please, I have no more space.
For sale: Bed. Do not use in the Nether.
Lost: One wolf named Rex. Last seen chasing a skeleton. If found, please give him a bone and my apologies.
Lost: Netherite pickaxe. Last seen falling into lava. Not expecting it back.
Lost: My sense of direction. Last seen in a jungle.
Found: One cat, very fluffy, very judgemental. Answers to "Peanut Butter" and the sound of fish.
Wanted: Brave adventurer to defeat the ender dragon. Must bring their own beds. Not for sleeping.

I used to be a miner, but I couldn't dig it. Now I'm just a minor inconvenience.
The cow was so good at math, it could moo-ltiply anything.
I gave my sheep a haircut and now it's feeling a little sheepish.
That creeper has a real explosive personality.
My pig started a band. He's the lead squealer.
The furnace and I have a warm relationship.
I'm reading a book about anti-gravity. It's impossible to put down. Unlike gravel.
That skeleton is a real bonehead, but he means well.
The bee and I are best friends. We're un-bee-lievably close.
My redstone circuit keeps breaking. It's having a power struggle.
I'd make a joke about TNT, but I'm afraid it would blow up.
Fishing is easy. You just have to get hooked on it.
The ghast is a real drama queen. Always making a scene.
That witch really knows how to brew trouble.
The iron golem is a real heavyweight in the village.
My diamond pickaxe has a lot of carat-er.
That enderman is so tall, he always looks down on people. Literally.
The zombie went to the gym, but he still felt dead tired.
The chicken told a joke, but it was a bit of a yolk.
The villager tried to be a comedian, but his jokes were always a bit "hrm".
The turtle was late again. He said he was just shell-shocked.
The slime was in a sticky situation.
My parrot is a real chatterbox. Polly wants a microphone.
The snow golem is chill. Literally.
The spider is a great web designer.
The fox stole my sword. Talk about a sly move.
That frog is so happy, he's practically hopping with joy.
The pufferfish is very full of himself.
The squid is a little inky today.
My wolf is very pawsitive about everything.
The cat purr-fected her nap schedule.
The horse has a stable personality.
The mooshroom is a fun-gi to be around.
The axolotl asked a lot of questions. He's very a-lot-l curious.
The bat is great at hanging out.
The panda is very bamboo-zled today.
The polar bear has an ice personality.
The goat really knows how to ram a point home.
The camel always gets over the hump.
The sniffer has a nose for trouble.
My shovel and I really dig each other.
The anvil was dropped from the team. It was too heavy.
The torch is the light of my life.
The bucket kicked the habit.
The compass always points me in the right direction, even when I don't want to go home.
The clock is always on time. It's a real watch-dog.
The map and I go way back. It knows where I've been.
The shield and I have a protective relationship.
The bow has a lot of tension in its life.
My bed and I have a deep relationship. We spend every night together.
The ladder helped me get to the next level.
The door and I have an open relationship. Mostly because I forgot to close it.
The crafting table always has something new on the table.
The brewing stand is always stirring up trouble.
The enchanting table is spellbinding.
The beacon really lights up a room.
The hopper is always taking things.
The piston keeps pushing my buttons.
The observer is always watching. Very nosy.

The jukebox has a great record.

The lectern is always reading too much into things.

The honey block is sweet but clingy.

The sponge soaks up all the drama.

The ice block is cool under pressure.
The obsidian is very hard to get to know.
The bedrock is the most grounded block I know.
The sand is a bit unstable. It keeps falling for things.
Cobblestone is the most common friend. Always around, never special, always there.
The glass is very transparent with its feelings.
The wool is very soft-spoken.
The emerald has a very green personality. Kind of envious.
The gold ingot shines in every situation.
Netherite is very resistant to change.
The ender pearl is always jumping to conclusions.
The eye of ender keeps an eye on everything.
The totem of undying always has your back. Once.
The trident is a fork-midable weapon.
The elytra really takes off in conversation.
The firework has a short fuse.
The spyglass sees right through you.
The bundle is very well organized. Unlike me.
The lead keeps everyone in line.
The name tag gives you an identity crisis.
The saddle is always ready for a ride.
The cake is a lie. Just kidding, it's delicious.
The cookie crumbles under pressure.
The pumpkin pie is very well rounded.
The golden apple is the apple of my eye.
The rotten flesh has seen better days.
The poisonous potato is just misunderstood.
The beetroot can't beet the competition.
The carrot keeps everyone on their toes. Especially rabbits.
The melon is one in a melon.
The baked potato is a hot topic.
The sweet berries are a little prickly.
The glow berries brighten my day.
The suspicious stew is very suspicious. Always.
Creeper confession: I don't actually want to explode. I just get really nervous around people.
Zombie confession: I don't even like brains. I just never learned to cook.
Skeleton confession: I miss on purpose. I'm a pacifist with a bow.
Enderman confession: I take blocks because I'm building a little house. Nobody ever asks about my house.
Villager confession: I know my prices are too high. I just like watching you think about it.
Ghast confession: I'm not sad. I just have allergies.
Witch confession: I can't actually brew. I buy everything from the wandering trader.
Spider confession: I'm scared of players. Please stop screaming when you see me.
Chicken confession: I fall slowly because I'm afraid of heights.
Pig confession: I never asked for a saddle.
Cow confession: I'm tired of people hitting me for leather. Try asking nicely.
Sheep confession: I like being dyed. Pink is my favorite.
Llama confession: I spit because nobody listens to me otherwise.
Piglin confession: I don't even like gold. I just want to be included.
Wither confession: I spin around because I'm trying to look cool. It's working.
Ender dragon confession: I'd let you have the egg if you just asked.
Warden confession: I'm actually very shy. I just want people to use their indoor voices.
Phantom confession: I don't want to attack you. I just want you to get some sleep.
Bee confession: I sting because I panic. I'm working on it.
Slime confession: I'm not sticky on purpose. It's a skin condition.
Iron golem confession: I'm not as tough as I look. I cry when kids hug me.
Fox confession: I steal things because I'm lonely and they're shiny.
Allay confession: I'm not helping you. I'm just really into collecting things.
Peanut Butter's confession: I knock things off the shelf because I like the sound. I'm not sorry.
Merl's confession: Sometimes I say "I don't know" just for the nostalgia.
A player's confession: I still don't know how redstone works. I copy everything from videos.
A builder's confession: Every one of my castles has at least one dirt block hidden somewhere.
A miner's confession: I've dug straight down. More than once. Don't tell anyone.
An explorer's confession: I'm not exploring. I'm lost and I'm too proud to admit it.
A farmer's confession: I don't actually like carrots. I just like watching them grow.
Dating profile, Creeper: "Looking for someone to get close to. Must like surprises. Allergic to cats."
Dating profile, Enderman: "Tall, mysterious, collects blocks. Please don't stare on the first date."
Dating profile, Zombie: "Night owl. Loves long walks in the dark. Hates sunny days. Not a vegetarian."
Dating profile, Skeleton: "Great shot (citation needed). Very bony. Will rattle your world."
Dating profile, Villager: "Successful businessman. Owns a house and one job block. Says 'hrm' a lot."
Dating profile, Ghast: "Big, sensitive, loud. Looking for someone who can handle a few tears."
Dating profile, Iron Golem: "Strong, protective, gives flowers. Looking for a village to call home."
Dating profile, Witch: "Good at potions. Bad at relationships. Swipe right if you like purple."
Dating profile, Pig: "Pink, round, loves carrots. Looking for someone who won't put a saddle on me."
Dating profile, Llama: "Fluffy, honest, will spit if necessary. Not looking for a trader."
Dating profile, Ender Dragon: "Looking for a challenger. Must bring their own arrows. No beds please."
Dating profile, Warden: "Quiet nights in. Loves listening. Hates loud people. Blind dates only."
Dating profile, Bee: "Busy, sweet, a little intense. Looking for someone who likes flowers."
Dating profile, Cat: "Independent. Fluffy. Will sit on your stuff. Scares away creepers for free."
Dating profile, Axolotl: "Smiley, pink, loves water. Will help in a fight. Must love fish."
Dating profile, Wolf: "Loyal, fluffy, loves bones. Looking for my forever player."
Dating profile, Snow Golem: "Cool personality. Melts easily. Prefers cold climates."
Dating profile, Sniffer: "Ancient, curious, big nose. Looking for someone who digs old things."
Dating profile, Shulker: "Shy, lives in a box, likes levitating people. Opens up slowly."
Dating profile, Peanut Butter: "Not looking. Already have Merl. She's acceptable."
I'm not saying my base is big, but I need a minecart to get to the kitchen.
I'm not saying I'm bad at building, but my house has been mistaken for a creeper crater twice.
I'm not saying I'm a hoarder, but I have a chest just for chests.
I'm not saying I'm lost, but my compass just shrugged.
I'm not saying I'm afraid of the dark, but my mine has more torches than walls.
I'm not saying I play too much, but my cat has started meowing in villager.
I'm not saying my farm is big, but the rabbits have formed a government.
I'm not saying I'm unlucky, but even my fishing rod catches boots on purpose.
I'm not saying the villager is greedy, but he charged me for saying "hello".
I'm not saying the Nether is hot, but my potion of fire resistance is sweating.
I'm not saying I've died a lot, but my grave has a guest book.
I'm not saying the warden is loud, but my ears are still ringing from last week.
I'm not saying Peanut Butter is spoiled, but she has her own enchanted bed.
I'm not saying I'm bad at redstone, but my lights turn on when I open the door. I wanted the opposite.
I'm not saying my horse is slow, but the turtle offered it a ride.
I'm not saying the skeleton is a bad shot, but it just hit itself.
I'm not saying I love diamonds, but I named my children Pickaxe and Sword.
I'm not saying the End is empty, but even the echo left.
I'm not saying my house is small, but the bed and I have to take turns.
I'm not saying my sense of direction is bad, but I once got lost in my own bathroom.
Fortune cookie: You will find diamonds soon. Unless you're looking.
Fortune cookie: A great adventure awaits. Bring food. And a bed. Not in the Nether.
Fortune cookie: Someone close to you is hiding something. It's probably a creeper.
Fortune cookie: Today is a good day to build. Tomorrow is a good day to fix what you built.
Fortune cookie: You will meet a tall, dark stranger. Don't look him in the eyes.
Fortune cookie: Your luck will change. Mostly when you're near lava.
Fortune cookie: Patience is a virtue. So is a water bucket.
Fortune cookie: Good things come to those who wait. Especially sapling growth.
Fortune cookie: The answer you seek is deeper than you think. Around Y -59.
Fortune cookie: You will soon receive a gift. It's a poppy from an iron golem.
Fortune cookie: Beware of green things that hiss.
Fortune cookie: A friend will help you today. Her name is Merl.
Fortune cookie: You will travel far. Your horse will not.
Fortune cookie: Your next big project will be bigger than planned. They always are.
Fortune cookie: Don't count your chickens before they hatch. Or after. There are too many.
Fortune cookie: The stars say you'll find treasure. The stars don't say where.
Fortune cookie: Today you'll make a great trade. Tomorrow you'll realize it wasn't.
Fortune cookie: A cat will choose you. You don't get a say in this.
Fortune cookie: Your elytra flight will end well, if you remember the water bucket.
Fortune cookie: Fortune favors the bold. Lava favors the careless.
Life advice: Never dig straight down. Never dig straight up. Honestly, digging is dangerous.
Life advice: If your house is too quiet, check for a warden. Then check again.
Life advice: Always carry a stack of food. Hunger is the real final boss.
Life advice: Label your chests. Future you will thank you. Future you will still forget to look.
Life advice: Every creeper is a chance to practice running.
Life advice: Don't trust a pressure plate in a temple.
Life advice: If a villager offers you a deal that's too good to be true, it's probably for sticks.
Life advice: Always build a door. Even if the zombies can break it, it's the thought that counts.
Life advice: When lost, follow a river. Rivers lead to oceans, and oceans lead to more confusion.
Life advice: If you can't beat the ender dragon, try again tomorrow. It's not going anywhere.
Life advice: A good base has three things: a bed, a chest, and a way to escape from the bed and the chest.
Life advice: Pet your cat. Pet your dog. Pet Peanut Butter. Pets make everything better.
Life advice: Take breaks. The world will still be there. The creepers too, unfortunately.
Life advice: If you don't know, ask Merl. If Merl doesn't know, ask the wiki. If the wiki doesn't know, ask #user-help.
Life advice: Sometimes the best build is the one you finish.
Life advice: A torch in the right place is worth ten in your inventory.
Life advice: Don't look back. There might be an enderman.
Life advice: The best defense is a moat. The second best is a cat.
Life advice: Respect the bees and they'll respect you. Mostly.
Life advice: Never sleep in the End. You won't wake up rested.
Overheard in the village: "Hrm." "Hrm?" "Hrm." "Oh, that's terrible."
Overheard in the village: "Did you see the new player? They took my bed." "Again?"
Overheard in the village: "I raised the price of bread." "Why?" "Because I can."
Overheard in the village: "The golem gave me a flower today." "He gives everyone a flower." "I know, but it still felt special."
Overheard in the village: "Who keeps planting carrots in my wheat field?" "The rabbits are organizing."
Overheard in the village: "I heard there's a zombie siege tonight." "Lock your doors!" "We don't have locks." "...hrm."
Overheard in the village: "The wandering trader is back." "Hide the emeralds."
Overheard in the village: "Have you seen my cat?" "It's sitting on the player's chest." "Of course it is."
Overheard in the village: "Why does the player keep hitting the bell?" "He thinks it's a doorbell."
Overheard in the village: "I'm a librarian." "You've never read a book." "I'm a librarian in spirit."
Overheard in the Nether: "It's so cold today." "It's 2000 degrees." "Exactly, it's usually 3000."
Overheard in the Nether: "Is that a player?" "With gold armor?" "Never mind, he's one of us."
Overheard in the End: "Is anyone else here?" Endermen: "..." Dragon: "Just us."
Overheard in a cave: "Did you hear that?" "It's just a bat." "Bats don't hiss."
Overheard in a cave: "We should place more torches." "We placed 300." "Exactly. More."
Overheard at spawn: "Which way is north?" "The sun rises in the east." "It's night." "Then good luck."
Overheard at a farm: "The cows are staring at me." "They know what you did."
Overheard at the beach: "Look, a turtle!" Turtle: "Look, a player. Great. Leave my eggs alone."
Overheard at the ocean monument: "This is fine." *mining fatigue* "This is not fine."
Overheard in a stronghold: "Is this the portal room?" "No, it's the library." "Is this the portal room?" "No, it's another corridor."
Overheard on Discord: "Merl, how do I get a boss key?" Me: "I've been waiting for this moment my whole life."
Overheard at the help desk: "Where's my house?" Me: "Where did you build it?" "Near a tree." Me: "Which tree?" "A green one."
Overheard at the help desk: "Can you help me find diamonds?" Me: "Yes." "Where are they?" Me: "Underground." "Where underground?" Me: "Yes."
Overheard at the help desk: "Merl, are you a real person?" Me: "I'm a real help desk assistant." "That's not an answer." Me: "That's a help desk answer."
Overheard at the help desk: "What's the best enchantment?" Me: "Mending." "What's the second best?" Me: "Also Mending."
Overheard at the help desk: "Why did my house explode?" Me: "Were you near a creeper?" "Define 'near'."
Overheard at the help desk: "My cat won't move off my keyboard." Me: "Welcome to the club."
Overheard at the help desk: "How do I stop dying?" Me: "Have you tried not dying?" "Very funny." Me: "I'm serious, it really helps."
Overheard at the help desk: "Where's the Nether?" Me: "Through the portal." "Which portal?" Me: "The one you have to build." "Oh."
Overheard at the help desk: "Can Peanut Butter help me?" Peanut Butter: *yawns* Me: "That's a no."
A tiny poem: Roses are red, creepers are green. That was my house, now it's a ravine.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, the sky is blue. I dug straight down, and now I'm through.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, lava is too. I had a pickaxe. Now I have a clue.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, endermen are tall. I looked at one once. That's all.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, bones are white. The skeleton missed me all through the night.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, gold is bright. The piglins are angry, I opened a chest last night.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, the End is dark. The dragon is mean, but the elytra's a lark.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, bees are yellow. I hit the hive. Bad idea, fellow.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, my cat is grey. She sat on my keyboard and deleted my day.
A tiny poem: Roses are red, nights are long. I forgot my bed, and that was wrong.
A haiku: Hissing in the dark. A flash of green behind me. My house had a roof.
A haiku: Deep under the ground. Diamonds glitter next to lava. I just watch them burn.
A haiku: Villager stares on. Prices higher than mountains. Hrm, he says. Hrm, hrm.
A haiku: Sun rises slowly. Zombies burning in the field. Morning has broken.
A haiku: Peanut Butter sleeps. The keyboard is warm and soft. My work can wait now.
A haiku: The warden listens. I hold my breath for an hour. Someone sneezes. Oops.
A haiku: Elytra soaring. The ground is coming closer. Water bucket. Please.
A haiku: One more block, I said. Now the castle has a moat. And a dragon too.
A limerick: There once was a miner named Lee, who dug for a diamond or three. He found lava instead, went straight back to bed, and now he just mines in his tea.
A limerick: A creeper who lived on a hill would wander for fun and for thrill. He got close to a guy, said a sizzling goodbye, and the crater is out there still.
Job description, Creeper: "Demolition expert. Works alone. Very short contracts."
Job description, Enderman: "Freelance landscaper. Moves one block at a time. Prefers no eye contact with clients."
Job description, Skeleton: "Archer. Experience: lots. Accuracy: let's not talk about it."
Job description, Zombie: "Night shift security. Breaks down doors. Allergic to sunlight."
Job description, Villager: "Merchant. Sets prices based on mood. Says 'hrm' professionally."
Job description, Iron Golem: "Bodyguard. Gives flowers on breaks. Throws zombies very far."
Job description, Witch: "Pharmacist. Medicines may be poison. No refunds."
Job description, Cat: "Pest control. Scares creepers. Paid in fish and naps."
Job description, Allay: "Personal shopper. Brings you everything. Really, everything."
Job description, Bee: "Pollination specialist. Will sting if you insult the boss."
Job description, Wandering Trader: "Sales representative. Sells sand. Has two llama bodyguards."
Job description, Warden: "Librarian of the Deep Dark. Enforces quiet with extreme force."
Job description, Phantom: "Sleep consultant. Visits you when you stay up too late."
Job description, Ender Dragon: "Gatekeeper. Has held the same job for years. Excellent benefits. Terrible visitors."
Job description, Merl: "Help desk. Knows the wiki. Has a cat. Says 'I don't know' when it matters most."
Job description, Peanut Butter: "Supervisor. Sits on things. Approves nothing."
In Minecraft you can carry 2,000 blocks of stone in your pockets. In real life I can't carry the groceries in one trip.
In Minecraft you can build a house in one night. In real life I can't build a shelf without crying.
In Minecraft you heal by eating steak. In real life, steak only helps a little.
In Minecraft you can punch a tree until it gives you wood. In real life the tree wins.
In Minecraft night lasts seven minutes. In real life it lasts until I finish this one last episode.
In Minecraft you can fall 20 blocks into water and be fine. In real life, please don't try that.
In Minecraft you can sleep through a thunderstorm. In real life the thunder wins.
In Minecraft every cow drops leather. In real life you have to buy shoes.
In Minecraft you can tame a wolf with bones. In real life the wolf would just take the bones.
In Minecraft a villager will give you emeralds for paper. In real life my paper is worth nothing.
In Minecraft you can swim in lava with a potion. In real life, there is no potion. Don't swim in lava.
In Minecraft you can respawn at your bed. In real life you just wake up there.
In Minecraft the sun burns zombies. In real life it just burns me.
In Minecraft you can find diamonds by digging. In real life you find a pipe and a very angry neighbor.
In Minecraft you can plant a sapling and get a tree in minutes. In real life my basil died in a week.
In Minecraft you can climb a ladder while holding 64 anvils. In real life I get tired climbing stairs with a backpack.
In Minecraft you can move a whole mountain. In real life I can't even move my couch.
In Minecraft the map shows everything you've explored. In real life my map app shows a gas station.
In Minecraft you can store a whole ocean in a bucket. In real life my bucket has a hole in it.
In Minecraft you can write in a book and sign it forever. In real life I can't find a pen.
In Minecraft, a cat keeps the creepers away. In real life, a cat keeps the sleep away.
In Minecraft, you die and keep going. In real life, you just stub your toe and have to go lie down.
In Minecraft, a bed explodes in the Nether. In real life, my bed just has crumbs.
In Minecraft, I'm a brave adventurer. In real life, I'm scared of spiders the size of a coin.
In Minecraft, a cake has seven slices. In real life, a cake has one slice: all of it.

Warning label on an ender pearl: "Landing may hurt. Endermites not included, but possible."
Warning label on a fishing rod: "May catch boots."
Warning label on a cake: "Do not leave unattended near Peanut Butter."
Warning label on a pickaxe: "Do not use to dig straight down."
Warning label on elytra: "Fireworks sold separately. Ground included."
Warning label on a potion of invisibility: "Your armor is still visible. Everyone can see your floating boots."
Warning label on a saddle: "Pig must consent."
Warning label on a spawner: "May produce unexpected guests."
Warning label on a bell: "Ringing may summon an entire village."
Warning label on a shield: "Does not protect against falling, lava, or bad decisions."
Warning label on a goat horn: "Your neighbors will hear this. All of them."
Warning label on a compass: "Points to spawn. Not to your house. Never to your house."
Warning label on a map: "Not to scale. Not to be trusted."

Warning label on a beehive: "Contains bees. Very angry bees. Do not hit."

User manual for a villager: "Step 1: Trade. Step 2: Regret the trade. Step 3: Trade again."

User manual for a horse: "Step 1: Saddle. Step 2: Ride. Step 3: Get thrown off. Step 4: Try again with an apple."
User manual for the ender dragon: "Step 1: Destroy crystals. Step 2: Dodge breath. Step 3: Collect egg. Step 4: Feel bad, a little."
User manual for redstone: "Step 1: Connect. Step 2: Disconnect. Step 3: Watch a tutorial. Step 4: Give up and use a lever."
