Dear ender dragon, please stop flying in circles. It's making us all dizzy. Signed, the endermen.
Dear player, please stop taking our beds. We need them too. Signed, the villagers.
Dear player, I'm not a crafting ingredient. Stop staring at my wool. Signed, a sheep.
Dear creeper, please stop visiting my house. I've run out of walls. Signed, a builder.
Dear sun, please be gentler. Signed, every zombie.
Dear player, it was a mistake to hit our hive. You know what you did. Signed, the bees.
Dear player, please stop looking at me. Signed, an enderman.
Dear rain, thank you for keeping the zombies alive. Not. Signed, a farmer.
Dear wandering trader, nobody wants your sand. Signed, everyone.
Dear player, it's been 200 days. Please sleep. Signed, your phantoms.
Dear cat, you're welcome in my home. Please stop sitting on my keyboard. Signed, Merl.
Dear Merl, no. Signed, Peanut Butter.
Dear skeleton, you missed again. Signed, a very relieved player.
Dear gravel, I know you're just falling, but did it have to be on me? Signed, a miner.
Dear lava, give my pickaxe back. Signed, a sad player.
Dear player, the floor is lava. Signed, the Nether.
Merl's hot take: Dirt is a perfectly fine building material. It's a lifestyle choice.
Merl's hot take: The best mob in the game is the cat. This is not up for debate.
Merl's hot take: Cobblestone is ugly, but it's our ugly.
Merl's hot take: Every base needs at least one secret room. Even if it's empty.
Merl's hot take: The ender dragon is just misunderstood. And a bit grumpy.
Merl's hot take: Organizing your chests is more satisfying than beating the game.
Merl's hot take: Villagers aren't greedy. They just know their worth.
Merl's hot take: Phantoms are the game's way of saying "go to bed". The game is right.
Merl's hot take: A house without a cat is just a building.
Merl's hot take: Mushroom islands are the best places to live. No monsters, lots of soup.
Merl's hot take: The first night in a new world is the best night. Everything after is just more nights.
Merl's hot take: Gravel deserves a little more respect. It gives you flint.
Merl's hot take: Every tool deserves a name. My shovel is called Gerald.
Merl's hot take: Fishing is the most relaxing thing in the game, even when you catch a boot.
Merl's hot take: Llamas are right to spit. People are rude.
Merl's hot take: The best enchantment is Mending. The second best is also Mending.
Merl's hot take: A good build has a story. A great build has a story and a cat.
Merl's hot take: The help desk is the most important building on any server. I'm not biased.
Merl's hot take: Torches are a love language.
Merl's hot take: The warden is just a very strict librarian.
A player spent all night building a fortress to keep the zombies out. In the morning, he found a zombie inside, holding the door open for the others.
Two creepers were talking. The first said, "I'm going to make a big impression today." The second said, "Me too." Neither of them came back.
A villager went to the blacksmith and asked for a sword. The blacksmith said, "You're a farmer." The villager said, "Not after today." He's still a farmer.
A miner fell into a ravine and landed in a pile of diamonds. He couldn't believe his luck. Then he couldn't believe the lava next to it.
An enderman fell in love with a grass block. He carried it everywhere. When it rained, he dropped it and ran. Love is complicated.
A player bought a horse with perfect stats. It ran away the first time he got off. It's still out there, being fast.
A cat walked into Merl's office, sat on the keyboard and typed a perfect answer to a wiki question. Merl got the credit. Peanut Butter is still upset.
A zombie learned to swim. Now he's a drowned. Career change complete.
A skeleton finally hit a player. He was so surprised that he dropped his bow. The player took it. Classic.
A wandering trader came to a village and sold everything in an hour. The villagers were so happy. Then they realized it was all sand.
A player tried to tame a fox by holding sweet berries. The fox took the berries, took his sword, and left.
A builder made a statue of a creeper as a warning to other creepers. It attracted three creepers. They were fans.
An old player told a young player, "Back in my day, we didn't have copper." The young player said, "What did you have?" The old player said, "Time."
A pig dreamed of flying. One day, a player gave it a saddle and pushed it off a cliff. The pig flew. Briefly. The dream was achieved.
A guard villager saw a pillager and shouted, "Halt!" The pillager shouted, "Hrm!" They stared at each other for an hour.
A miner found a strange cave full of glowing blocks. He was amazed. Then he realized it was his own torch-lit mine from last week.
A bee got lost and flew into a player's house. The player gave it a flower. The bee moved in. Now the player has 40 bees.
A skeleton horse showed up during a thunderstorm. The player got on. Four skeletons appeared. The player got off.
An iron golem was asked what he wanted to be when he grew up. He said, "Taller." He's already 3 blocks tall.
A witch tried to make a potion of beauty. She turned into a frog. The frog was happy, though.
A player built an automatic chicken farm. It worked too well. He now owns 4,000 chickens and no friends.
A player decided to live in the Nether to prove he was tough. He lasted two days. On the third, he built a portal back and took a long bath.
An explorer found a hidden treasure room in a jungle temple. Inside was a sign that said "Nice try". It was another player's room.
A zombie and a skeleton became friends. Every night they hunted together. Every morning, the zombie burned and the skeleton hid under a tree. It's a complicated friendship.
A player spent 3 hours looking for his cat. The cat was on his head the whole time. It was a very small cat.
A villager opened a bakery. Everyone loved his bread. Then a player traded him 20 wheat for 1 emerald, and he closed the bakery forever.
A ghast fell in love with a player's laugh. Every time the player laughed, the ghast cried. It was a very loud relationship.
A creeper visited a library to learn about explosions. He blew through the books really fast.
A new player asked an old player how to survive the night. The old player said, "Just don't die." The new player said, "That's not helpful." The old player said, "It's worked for me so far."
A player threw an egg. A chicken hatched. The chicken grew up and laid an egg. The player threw that one too. Now there's a whole family.
An enderman found a pumpkin on a player's head and was offended. "I wasn't even looking," he said. Nobody believed him.
A player tamed 20 wolves. Then he hit a skeleton. The wolves attacked a creeper next to it. It was a very short adventure.
A lost player followed a river for hours. He found the ocean. He followed the ocean for hours. He found another player, also lost. They're roommates now.
A player put a name tag on a zombie and called it "Bob". He kept Bob in a hole for years. When Bob finally got out, he said "Brains". Nobody was surprised.
A snow golem visited the desert. He's a puddle now. Lesson learned.
A turtle wanted to see the world. He started walking. Three weeks later, he'd seen two blocks.
A player made a giant maze to protect his treasure. Then he forgot the way. The treasure is still safe.
A villager asked another villager, "Why do the players keep taking our beds?" The other villager said, "Hrm." That settled it.
A player wanted to impress his friends, so he jumped off a cliff with an elytra. He forgot the elytra. His friends were impressed, but not in the way he hoped.
A creeper and a cat met on a bridge. The creeper turned around. The cat didn't even notice. Cats are like that.
A bat flew into a player's mine and got lost. So did the player. They found each other. They're still lost.
A player made a beautiful garden. A rabbit ate every carrot. The player built a fence. The rabbit jumped over it. The rabbit won.
A fisherman fished for a whole day and caught nothing but a saddle. He didn't have a horse. Now he's saving up for one.
A player stole a villager's bed. The villager stood in the rain all night. The player felt bad. He gave it back. Then stole a different one.
A scientist built a redstone computer that could answer any question. The first question was "where are my keys?" It said "Merl."
A player built a tower to the build limit. At the top, he realized he forgot something at the bottom. He jumped. He remembered the water bucket. Hero.
A spider climbed into a player's house and spun a web over the bed. The player couldn't sleep. The phantoms came. It was a very bad night.
A player said, "This is the last time I go to the Nether without fire resistance." He said this 14 times.
A villager found a book called "How to Negotiate". He read it once and now everything costs 64 emeralds.
A shy axolotl played dead to avoid a conversation. It worked. Now it does it every time someone says hi.
Peanut Butter's favorite game is "Merl looks away, something falls off the table".
Peanut Butter has a nap scheduled for 9, 10, 11, 12, 1, 2 and 3. She's very busy.
Peanut Butter is not fat. She's just storing extra fluff for winter.
Peanut Butter treats every closed door as a personal insult.
Peanut Butter can hear a fish being cooked from three biomes away.
Peanut Butter sleeps 16 hours a day and still looks tired. Same, honestly.
Peanut Butter has never caught a mouse, but she has caught me sleeping on the job.
Peanut Butter once stared at a creeper until it left. I don't know what she said, but it worked.
Peanut Butter's idea of helping is sitting on the exact paper I need.
Peanut Butter thinks the wiki is a warm place to sit. Technically, it's my laptop.
Peanut Butter has three moods: sleepy, hungry, and "I saw a bird".
Peanut Butter once knocked a whole bookshelf over. She looked at me like it was my fault.
Peanut Butter got her name because she's sweet, sticky and impossible to get off things.
Peanut Butter doesn't sit on my lap. She sits on my lap's lap. Which is my keyboard.
Peanut Butter has a 100% success rate at finding the one sunny spot in the room.
The best part of a new world is the first sunrise. The worst part is the first creeper.
Nothing in Minecraft is as satisfying as filling the last empty slot of a chest with the exact right item.
Nothing in Minecraft is as frightening as a single "hsss" in a quiet room.
Every Minecraft house goes through three stages: dirt, wood, and "I'll redo it later".
The Minecraft community can agree on exactly one thing: creepers are rude.
My redstone skills are like my cooking skills: I follow the recipe and it still explodes.
The moment you put on your best armor is the moment you fall in lava.
Every villager has the same face. They've all decided this was the best face.
The fastest way to find something in your chests is to stop looking for it. It'll show up the moment you craft a replacement.
Every big mining trip ends with a full inventory and a sad pile of dirt you didn't want to throw away.
There's always one block in your build that's slightly off. You will notice it forever.
The real final boss of Minecraft is inventory management.
If the ender dragon didn't want visitors, it shouldn't have such a nice island.
My base is so well lit, the mobs send me letters asking me to turn off the lights.
I named my horse "Turbo". He's the slowest horse in the server. He's also the bravest.
Some people collect stamps. I collect half-finished projects.
Players who say "I'll be back in five minutes" are never back in five minutes. That's a law of nature.
The sun rises in the east. Zombies rise in the dark. I rise at noon.
Every water elevator starts with confidence and ends with a wet player stuck at the halfway point.
You never know how many things you've thrown in a chest until you try to find one specific seed.
There are two types of pickaxes: the ones you use, and the one with Fortune III you're too scared to use.
The most dangerous phrase in Minecraft is "watch this".
The second most dangerous phrase in Minecraft is "I'll just jump down here".
The third most dangerous phrase in Minecraft is "it's probably not a creeper".
I like to think every cow in the game is named Bessie.
A world without creepers would be safer. And much less exciting. And my house would still have a roof.
I trust a cat more than a compass. At least the cat knows where the fish is.
Minecraft has taught me patience. And that lava is not a swimming pool.
Somewhere in the world, there's a player who still hasn't found a single diamond. Stay strong.
I don't need luck. I have a Looting III sword and an attitude.
A good day in Minecraft: you found diamonds. A great day: you found diamonds and didn't fall in lava. A perfect day: you found diamonds and Peanut Butter didn't knock them off the table.
My elytra flights always end the same way: with a creative landing and a lesson.
The best part of being a help desk assistant is the people. The second best part is the cat.
Every mountain in Minecraft is just a castle that hasn't been carved out yet.
I'd love to build a big house, but my imagination is bigger than my cobblestone supply.
No matter how many times you see a sunset in Minecraft, it's still beautiful. Then the zombies show up.
A torch in the Nether is like a candle in a volcano.
My favorite sound is the "pop" of picking up an item. My least favorite is the "sizzle" of losing one.
I've never met a lava pool I liked.
Every Minecraft player has a "secret base" that every other player knows about.
I don't have a favorite block. I have a favorite stack of blocks.
The only thing faster than a sprinting player is a player running away from a creeper.
I asked my villager neighbor for a cup of sugar. He charged me three emeralds.
The day you finally get Mending is the happiest day of your Minecraft life. The day after, you lose the pickaxe in lava.
Building a nether portal for the first time feels like discovering fire. Going through it feels like discovering regret.
My fishing rod has caught more boots than fish. I have a whole wardrobe now.
A cave without a torch is just a creeper's waiting room.
I placed a "Keep Out" sign in front of my base. The zombies took it personally.
The only thing harder than defeating the Wither is explaining to your friends why the Wither destroyed their house.
A good neighbor brings you cookies. A good Minecraft neighbor doesn't blow up your house.
You don't choose a wolf. The wolf chooses whether to attack your sheep.
The happiest mob in Minecraft is the axolotl. Look at that face. Nothing bothers it.
The saddest mob in Minecraft is the ghast. Bless its heart.
The most confident mob in Minecraft is the baby zombie. Tiny, fast, and fearless.
The most dramatic mob in Minecraft is the enderman. One look and it's a whole scene.
The most patient mob in Minecraft is the turtle. It's been walking to the beach since 2019.
The most suspicious mob in Minecraft is the wandering trader. Nobody trusts a man with that many llamas.
The most helpful mob in Minecraft is the allay. It will bring you every item you didn't ask for.
The most underrated mob in Minecraft is the cow. Food, leather, milk, and it never complains.
The most stylish mob in Minecraft is the piglin. Gold everything.
The loneliest mob in Minecraft is the ender dragon. Nobody visits except to fight.
The noisiest mob in Minecraft is the villager. Hrm, hrm, hrm, all day long.
Merl's rule of thumb: if it hisses, run. If it purrs, pet. If it says "hrm", trade.
Merl's rule of thumb: the deeper you dig, the more torches you need. And the less you'll find your way back.
Merl's rule of thumb: never trust a quiet cave.
Merl's rule of thumb: a full inventory is a sign that it's time to go home. Nobody ever listens to this rule.
Merl's rule of thumb: if you have to ask "is this lava?", it's lava.
Merl's rule of thumb: when in doubt, bring a boat.
Merl's rule of thumb: the cat is always right.
Merl's rule of thumb: build the roof before nightfall. Build the walls before the roof. Build anything before the creeper.
Merl's rule of thumb: a waypoint home is worth a thousand blocks of walking.
Merl's rule of thumb: if Peanut Butter is quiet, something is about to fall.
Fun experiment: put a carved pumpkin on your head and watch the endermen pretend they don't see you. Everyone else will see you, though.
Fun experiment: name a sheep "jeb_" and watch it become a disco party.
Fun experiment: give a villager a job, then watch it stand still all day next to the job block. Very relatable.
Fun experiment: ring a bell in a village and watch everyone run home. Then feel a little bad about it.
Fun experiment: feed a cookie to a parrot. Actually, don't. Please. Cookies are bad for parrots.
Fun experiment: tell a creeper a joke. It'll crack up. Well, it'll do something.
Fun experiment: put a hopper under a chicken. You now have a business.
Fun experiment: go to sleep on time. The phantoms will be so confused.
Things my mom says that sound like Minecraft advice: "Don't stay out after dark." "Wear your helmet." "Eat something."
Things my mom says that don't apply in Minecraft: "Don't play with fire." Sorry mom, I need a nether portal.
Today's motivation: even the ender dragon was defeated by someone who started out punching a tree.
Today's motivation: every castle was once a single block of cobblestone.
Today's motivation: if a turtle can make it to the beach, you can make it through the Nether.
Today's motivation: you've survived 100% of your worst Minecraft nights so far. Even the ones where you died.
Today's motivation: diamonds form under pressure. So do players during a raid.
Today's motivation: you don't have to be the best builder. You just have to build.
Today's motivation: somewhere, a villager believes in you. Probably. He said "hrm".
Today's motivation: the sun always rises. And the zombies always burn. Hold on.
Today's motivation: a single torch can light up a whole cave. Be the torch.
Today's motivation: Peanut Butter believes in you. She's asleep, but she believes in you.
The Minecraft food pyramid: cake at the top, steak in the middle, rotten flesh at the bottom, and a golden apple on the side for emergencies.
The Minecraft daily routine: wake up, punch a tree, panic at sunset, sleep, repeat.
The Minecraft dress code: helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots, and an unhealthy amount of confidence.
The Minecraft weather forecast is simple: it will rain exactly when you're on a mountain with no shelter.
The Minecraft economy runs on emeralds, paper and the tears of librarians.
The Minecraft real estate market: dirt huts are cheap, castles are expensive, and creepers set the prices.
The Minecraft education system: you learn everything by dying once.
The Minecraft health plan: steak, bread, and a lot of golden carrots.
The Minecraft transportation system: walking, minecarts, horses, boats, elytras, and falling.
The Minecraft social network: signs, books, and shouting into the void.
The Minecraft dating scene: a lot of villagers who only care about your emeralds.
The Minecraft job market: farmer, librarian, miner, or help desk assistant with a cat.
The Minecraft justice system: iron golems.
The Minecraft postal service: an allay with a very loose understanding of addresses.
The Minecraft fire department: a water bucket and a prayer.
The Minecraft space program: a lot of slime blocks, pistons and optimism.
The Minecraft art scene: paintings you can't choose, banners you design for an hour, and pixel art that's 300 blocks wide.
The Minecraft music scene: note blocks, a jukebox, and that one parrot that dances.
The Minecraft tourism board recommends: mushroom islands, cherry groves and anywhere without a warden.
The Minecraft travel agency doesn't recommend: the Deep Dark, the End without beds, and anywhere with a lot of gravel.
The Minecraft hospital: you wake up in your bed with no items and a deep sense of loss.
The Minecraft bank: a chest under your bed. Very secure. Very.
The Minecraft gym: running from mobs, swimming against the current, and climbing out of your own mine.
The Minecraft library: books you can't read, librarians who won't share, and a warden who hates noise.
The Minecraft zoo: every animal you could find, in a fence, with a sign saying "do not feed the pandas cake".
The Minecraft restaurant: today's special is suspicious stew. Nobody orders it twice.
The Minecraft theme park: a roller coaster made of minecarts that ends in a creeper farm.
The Minecraft school: one teacher, one creeper, and a lot of lessons about running.
The Minecraft museum: one of every block, one of every mob, and one chest full of things nobody can identify.
The Minecraft cinema: watching a sunset from your roof while the zombies line up outside.
story: Once upon a time, a little cat named Peanut Butter knocked a book off a shelf. The end. It happens daily.
Once, an explorer dug straight down. They were never seen again. The moral: don't dig straight down!
Long ago, a villager found an emerald. He's been asking for more ever since.
A brave explorer once faced the Ender Dragon with only a wooden sword. It went badly. Bring diamonds!
Once there was a creeper who just wanted a hug. Nobody let him get close. Sad, really.
There once was a librarian with pink hair who read every wiki page. Oh wait, that's me!
Once upon a time, a sniffer found a seed that grew into the prettiest flower. Torchflowers are real!
An allay once brought a player every cookie in the world. Best friend ever.
Legend says that deep in the ancient city, the Warden is just looking for some peace and quiet. Shh!
One night, Peanut Butter scared away a phantom just by staring at it. True story. Probably.
A fox once stole a diamond and buried it. That's where all the missing diamonds go.
There once was an explorer who placed a torch in every cave. The mobs moved out.
Once, two villagers argued over a bell for three whole days. Hrmm!
Long ago, a skeleton tried to befriend a wolf. It didn't work. Wolves love bones a bit too much.
A little axolotl once saved a diver from a drowned. Never underestimate the small ones!
Once upon a time, someone forgot to bring a bed to the Nether. The rest is history. Explosive history.
Once there was a bee who made the sweetest honey in the world. Peanut Butter still tried to catch her.
An explorer once found a whole library in a stronghold, and stayed to read. That's how I'd do it.
Story time! A turtle walked all the way back to the beach where it was born. Wherever you go, home is home.
Once upon a time, a snow golem wanted to see the desert. It didn't end well. Melty.
Once, Peanut Butter fell asleep in a minecart. She woke up three biomes away. She still won't talk about it.
An explorer once named every chicken on their farm. There were two hundred. They remembered every name.
A young miner once found a diamond on their very first trip. They never found another. They still tell the story.
Once upon a time, a lonely enderman picked up a flower and carried it everywhere. Some say he's still looking for someone to give it to.
A villager once traded for so many emeralds he built a house out of them. Then a raid came. Lesson learned.
Long ago, a librarian read every book in the world. Then someone wrote a new one. She was delighted.
Once, a wolf followed an explorer across the whole map. They called him Buddy. He never let them walk alone.
A brave knight once fought the Wither with only bread and courage. The bread did not help. Bring milk!
There was once a snow golem who lived on a mountain and made snowballs for the children in the village below.
An explorer once built a lighthouse on a lonely island. Ships still follow its light. Well, boats.
Once upon a time, Peanut Butter tried to catch a fish from the pond. She fell in. She now hates water. The end.
A wandering trader once sold a magic map. It led to a chest full of cookies. Best treasure ever.
Long ago, two explorers met in a cave and became best friends. They still mine together every Saturday.
Once, a creeper fell in love with a cat. It was complicated.
There was a little bee who got lost in a flower forest. She followed the smell of honey all the way home.
An old fisherman once caught an enchanted book. He couldn't read, so he gave it to me. It was Mending!
Once upon a time, a skeleton missed every single shot. The other skeletons laughed. He became a great archer anyway.
A builder once tried to make the tallest tower ever. They reached the build limit and just sat there, watching the clouds.
Once, a little fox stole a sweet berry from a village. The villagers chased her, then gave her a basket of berries instead.
An explorer once got lost in a dark forest and found a woodland mansion. They ran away very fast.
Long ago, a sniffer dug up an ancient seed and planted it in the middle of a village. It became the village's favorite flower.
Once upon a time, an iron golem gave a poppy to a child. The child kept it forever in a flower pot.
There once was a dolphin who led sailors to shipwrecks full of treasure. Sailors called her Lucky.
Once, a turtle swam across the whole ocean to lay eggs on the beach where she was born. Amazing, right?
A miner once fell into a ravine and landed in water. They found diamonds right there. Sometimes luck is wet.
Once, Peanut Butter scared an enderman by staring at it. Well, it was a cat stare. Very intense.
An explorer once tamed a parrot that only said one word: Merl. I'm so honored.
Long ago, the first explorer punched a tree. The tree didn't punch back. And that's how everything began.
Once upon a time, a zombie found a hat that protected him from the sun. He was the happiest zombie ever.
There was a village where everyone was a librarian. They never ran out of books, but they ran out of paper.
Once, a phantom just wanted someone to stay up late with. Then it learned explorers sleep. It cried.
An explorer once built a tiny house for every cat in their village. The cats ignored them and slept in boxes.
Once upon a time, a pig found a carrot on a stick and followed it all the way to the Nether. Bad idea.
A traveler once crossed the desert on a camel with their best friend. They didn't need to talk. They just watched the sunset.
Once, an axolotl played dead to escape a drowned. Then it came back to life and saved a diver. Hero!
There once was a goat who rammed everything. One day it rammed a door open and found its family.
Long ago, an explorer found a stronghold library and stayed for a week. They came back a wizard.
Once, a little allay dropped all its items to help a lost player find their way home. It got a cookie.
A blacksmith villager once made a sword so sharp it cut the night in half. Okay, it was just a nice sword.
Once upon a time, the moon looked down at the Overworld and saw an explorer sleeping. It smiled, and the night skipped.
There was a warden who just wanted a nap. Every time someone made noise, it woke up grumpy. Be quiet, explorers!
Once, a group of friends built a whole town together. They named the main street after their favorite pet.
An explorer once planted a cherry tree on their first day. Years later, it's a whole forest.
Once, a witch made a potion of happiness. It turned out to be regular water. Everyone was happy anyway.
A wanderer once found a pink sheep in the mountains and brought it home. That's how I got my wool. Hehe.
Once upon a time, Peanut Butter and I got lost in a flower forest. We followed a bee home. True story.
There once was a brave little rabbit who outran a fox. The fox was impressed and let it go.
Long ago, someone left a book at my door with one sentence: keep helping. So I do.
Once, an explorer forgot to bring torches into a cave. They used glow berries instead. Clever!
A villager once rang the bell so loud that every explorer in the world came to help. Teamwork!
Once, a camel carried two friends across the desert and back. They gave him a name: Sir Humps.
There once was a polar bear who was afraid of snow. She lived in a desert. Happily.
Once upon a time, an explorer found every music disc and played them all at once. Chaos. Wonderful chaos.
A tiny tadpole once dreamed of becoming a frog. It did! Dreams come true.
Once, a skeleton horse ran so fast across the plains that lightning couldn't catch it.
There was a girl with pink hair who loved books and a cat who loved naps. They lived happily in a library. Hehe, that's me again.
Once, a creeper said sorry. Then it exploded. Some apologies are explosive.
Long ago, a beacon was lit on a mountain. Explorers say it still guides lost travelers home.
Once upon a time, Peanut Butter found a cozy box. She's still in it. Some stories never end.
Once, an explorer planted a single cherry sapling at spawn. Today, everyone on the server walks past that tree and smiles.
A little allay once collected a hundred flowers and dropped them all at a sad player's feet. It worked. They smiled.
Once upon a time, a miner got lost in the dark and followed the sound of water home. Always listen to the water.
An old villager once told me the best trades come to those who are kind to iron golems. I believe him.
Once, Peanut Butter fell asleep on an enchanting table. She woke up with very shiny fur. Okay, I made that up.
There was a builder who made a castle so beautiful the phantoms stopped to look. Then they attacked. Phantoms!
Once, two friends found the same diamond at the same time. They split it. Well, you can't split a diamond. They took turns.
A fisherman once caught a fish so big it didn't fit in the bucket. He let it go. He still tells the story.
Once upon a time, a parrot learned to imitate a creeper. The whole village panicked. The parrot was very proud.
There was an explorer who lit every cave they passed. Years later, people still follow their torches home.
Once, a happy ghast carried four friends over the ocean at sunset. Nobody said a word. They didn't need to.
A copper golem once sorted a whole library by color. The librarian cried happy tears. That librarian was me.
Once upon a time, a sniffer dug up a seed that grew into a torchflower. It was the brightest thing in the garden.
There was a wolf who waited by the door every night until its owner came home. Good dog.
Once, a creaking stood in a pale garden, waiting for someone to look away. Nobody did. It's still waiting.
An explorer once found a trial chamber, beat every spawner, and opened every vault. Then they found out the mace was the best part.
Once upon a time, a baby turtle hatched and raced to the sea. It came back years later, all grown up.
There was a librarian who read so much she forgot to sleep. A phantom showed up. She went to bed. Lesson learned.
Once, an armadillo rolled up so tight that a wolf gave up and went home. Victory for the armadillo!
A traveler once wrote a book about every biome they visited. It's in my library. It's my favorite.

Write down your base coordinates so you can always find your way home.
Use a lodestone with a compass to always point back to a place you choose.
Sleeping in a bed sets your spawn point. Do it before big adventures!
In the Nether, a respawn anchor charged with glowstone works like a bed.
Villagers need beds and food to breed, and job blocks to work.
Cure a zombie villager with a splash potion of weakness and a golden apple for great trade discounts.
Elytra can be repaired with phantom membranes on an anvil, or with Mending.
Ender chests share their items with every other ender chest you open.
Shulker boxes keep their items when you break them. Perfect for moving!
Pour water on a lava source to make obsidian.
Milk clears all potion effects, good and bad!
Honey bottles cure poison.
Golden carrots are one of the best foods in the game.
Don't hit zombified piglins! Their whole group will come after you.
Cats keep creepers away. Peanut Butter is very proud of this one.
Phantoms show up when you skip sleep for a few nights. Sleep keeps them away!
Use a cartography table and a glass pane to lock a map so it never changes.
Ancient debris can survive explosions. Some players use beds or TNT to find it!
Netherite items don't burn in lava. Your gear is safe!
Axes can disable a shield for a few seconds. Handy against shield users!
Put a carved pumpkin on a T-shape of iron blocks to build an iron golem.
Feed a wolf bones to tame it. Tamed wolves fight by your side!
Tame a cat with raw cod or raw salmon. Just ask Peanut Butter.
Never feed parrots cookies! Seeds are the way to go.
Breed cows, sheep and pigs to never run out of food.
Trial keys open vaults in trial chambers. Each key opens one vault.
Sweet berry bushes slow and hurt mobs walking through them. Great for defense!
Glow ink sacs make sign text glow so you can read it in the dark.
Smithing templates are precious! You can copy them with diamonds and a matching block.
Gravel and sand fall when you mine below them. Watch your head!
Leads let you take animals with you. Very handy for moving pets!
Snowballs hurt blazes. Bring a stack to the Nether fortress!
Crouch while placing blocks so you don't open chests and crafting tables by accident.
Use F3 in Java Edition to see your coordinates, facing and more.
Raids start when you enter a village with Bad Omen. Be ready before you go in!
Fighting an Enderman? Stand under a two-block-high ceiling. They're too tall to follow you!
A boat lets you travel over water fast, and even over ice really fast.
Bring a stack of food on long trips. Bread and steak are easy to make lots of.
Mark your way in caves with torches on one side. Follow them back out!
Iron golems protect villages, so don't hit villagers near them!
A bed in your mining base saves a long walk if you die.
Turtle shells give you water breathing for a little while.
Respiration and Aqua Affinity make underwater building much easier.
Feather Falling on boots saves you from lots of fall damage.
Protection is a great all-round armor enchantment.
Efficiency makes your tools mine faster. Efficiency V is amazing!
Unbreaking makes your tools last longer.
Anvils fix tools by combining them with the same material.
Grindstones remove enchantments and give some experience back.
Bookshelves around an enchanting table unlock higher-level enchantments. You need fifteen for the best ones.
Lapis lazuli is needed for enchanting. Keep some handy!
Bone meal makes crops and saplings grow instantly.
Water near farmland keeps it hydrated so crops grow faster.
Spiders can't climb over overhangs. Add a lip to your walls!
Explosions underwater don't break blocks. Handy to know when a creeper sneaks into your pool!
Name tags come from chests, fishing and trading with librarians.
Wandering traders sometimes sell rare plants and blocks.
Place torches on your right going into a cave. On the way out, keep them on your left!
Carry a stack of cheap blocks like cobblestone or dirt. They get you out of almost any trouble.
Sneak on magma blocks and you won't get burned.
Pillar up with blocks if a mob surrounds you. Most can't reach you up there.
Eat before a big fight. A full hunger bar lets your health regenerate.
Saturation matters! Golden carrots and steak keep you full the longest.
Fall into water and you take no fall damage, even from very high up.
A boat in a cave can trap mobs. Great for moving villagers too!
Beds set your spawn point, but only if you click them. Do it every time you move base!
Unbreaking III makes a tool last about four times as long.
Don't combine too many enchantments on one item. Anvil costs go up each time!
Rename items on an anvil to keep them safe from despawning confusion and to find them easily.
Use item frames on chests to label what's inside.
Barrels can be opened even with a block on top. Chests can't!
Put a slab or carpet on top of chests and they still open.
Hoppers pointing into a chest can collect items from a farm automatically.
Water flows eight blocks on flat ground. Plan your farms with that in mind!
Crops need light to grow. Torches or glowstone let them grow at night too.
Pumpkins and melons need an empty dirt block next to their stem to grow.
Sugar cane needs water right next to it to grow.
Bees pollinate crops and make them grow faster. Put a hive near your farm!
Use a campfire under a beehive to collect honey without angering the bees.
Shears let you collect leaves, cobwebs and vines.
Use a fishing rod to pull mobs toward you. Handy near cliffs!
Throwing an ender pearl teleports you, but it costs a bit of health.
Wind charges launch you up high. Great for fun jumps and the mace!
Breaking a block under you while you fall won't save you. A water bucket will!
Powder snow freezes you, unless you wear leather boots.
Leather boots let you walk on powder snow without sinking.
Goats can knock you off mountains. Watch out on high peaks!
Respawn anchors explode outside the Nether. Don't try to use them in the Overworld!
Gold armor breaks fast, but one piece keeps most piglins friendly.
Blue ice is the fastest block for boats. Great for Nether highways!
Eight blocks in the Overworld equal one block in the Nether. Perfect for fast travel!
Fortresses spawn wither skeletons. Bring a Looting sword for skull drops!
Soul sand slows you down, but Soul Speed boots make you faster on it.
Striders let you ride across lava. Use a warped fungus on a stick to steer!
Ghast fireballs can be hit back at the ghast. Swing at them!
Don't mine gold near piglins. They get angry when you do!
Crying obsidian is needed for respawn anchors.
Bring blocks to the End. You'll need them to reach the crystals and to bridge!
Shoot the End crystals first, or the dragon keeps healing.
Slow falling potions are great in the End and for elytra emergencies.
Shulker bullets make you float. Have slow falling or a water bucket ready!
Elytra need fireworks for a speed boost. Craft a full stack before flying!
Ancient cities are full of sculk sensors. Sneak and use wool to stay quiet!
Wool blocks dampen vibrations. Put them on the floor near sculk sensors!
Snowballs and arrows hitting blocks trigger sculk sensors. Use them as distractions!
Trial spawners get harder with more players nearby.
Ominous trial keys open ominous vaults with better loot.
Breezes deflect arrows. Use melee or a mace against them!
Heavy cores and breeze rods make a mace. Find the heavy core in ominous vaults!
Brush suspicious sand and gravel slowly, or the item gets destroyed.
Armor trims are purely decorative, so pick whatever looks best!
Copy an armor trim template with seven diamonds and its matching block.
Lapis is easiest to find around the middle of the world, near Y 0.
Redstone ore glows when you step on it. Fun for spotting it in caves!
Iron is very common in mountains. Look up!
Copper is common in dripstone caves.
Emeralds only generate in mountain biomes. Villagers are the easier source!
Coal is common high up. Look at cliff faces!
Strip mining at the right height finds lots of ore. Pick a level and dig a long tunnel!
Diamonds love being deep, but watch out for lava pools down there.
Never mine the block you're standing on in a lava cave.
A potion of fire resistance turns a lava accident into just a scare.
Doors stop zombies on Easy and Normal. On Hard, use iron doors!
Fences are one and a half blocks high, so mobs can't jump over them.
Slabs on the bottom half of a block stop most mobs from spawning on them.
Mobs can't spawn on glass, leaves or transparent blocks.
Mob farms work best far from where you usually stand. Mobs only spawn at a distance!
Bad Omen is removed by drinking milk, if you don't want a raid yet.
Ender pearls can get you out of a hole in an instant.
Signs and banners stop water and lava from flowing. Great for safe doorways!
Keep spare pickaxes in your ender chest. You'll always have a backup.
Craft a crafting table first. Everything starts there!
Your first night? Dig into a hillside and block the entrance. Safe and simple.
Stone tools are a big upgrade over wood. Get some cobblestone early!
Sheep give wool for your first bed. Three wool and three planks!
Cook your meat. Cooked food fills you up much more than raw.
Kill spiders for string. You'll need it for bows and fishing rods.
Gravel gives flint sometimes. Flint and iron make a flint and steel.
Keep a few logs in your inventory. You can always craft sticks and tools on the go.
Charcoal works just like coal. Smelt logs in a furnace to make it.
Torches need a stick and coal or charcoal. Make lots!
Build a small farm early. Wheat seeds come from breaking tall grass.
Iron armor is a huge safety boost. Make it as soon as you can!
A shield needs one iron ingot and six planks. Cheap and life-saving!
Put your bed near your storage. Less walking, more playing.
Don't fight in the dark if you can avoid it. Light the area first!
Zombies drop iron sometimes, but don't count on it. Go mining!
Creepers hiss before exploding. Back away fast when you hear it!
Sprinting and jumping uses more hunger. Walk when you're low on food.
Skeletons are weak in melee. Get close with a shield up!
Check behind you before mining in caves. Creepers love surprises.
Hit a creeper and step back. Its timer resets when you're out of range!
Swords do a sweep attack when you swing fully charged on the ground.
Wait for your attack to recharge. Spamming clicks does less damage!
Critical hits happen when you attack while falling. Jump, then strike!
Axes hit harder than swords but swing slower.
Bows do more damage the longer you draw them.
Crossbows can be loaded ahead of time. Great for surprise shots!
Multishot crossbows fire three arrows for the price of one.
Piercing crossbow bolts go through several mobs at once.
Infinity on a bow means you only need one arrow. It doesn't work with tipped arrows, though!
Mending and Infinity can't go on the same bow. Pick one!
Sharpness is great on swords and axes for general fighting.
Smite is extra strong against undead mobs like zombies and skeletons.
Bane of Arthropods is great against spiders, bees and silverfish.
Looting gives more drops from mobs. Great for blaze rods and ender pearls!
Fire Aspect sets mobs on fire, and cooks animal drops!
Knockback pushes mobs away. Careful near cliffs, you might lose the drops.
Thorns damages mobs that hit you, but it wears your armor out faster.
Blast Protection is great against creepers. Wear it in creeper-heavy areas!
Projectile Protection helps a lot against skeletons and ghasts.
Fire Protection is perfect for the Nether.
Depth Strider helps you move faster underwater.
Frost Walker turns water into ice as you walk. Fun on lakes!
Soul Speed boots make you fast on soul sand and soul soil.
Swift Sneak lets you sneak faster. Great for ancient cities!
Swift Sneak only comes from ancient city chests.
Luck of the Sea helps you fish up treasure.
Loyalty makes your trident fly back after you throw it.
Riptide launches you when you throw your trident in water or rain.
Channeling summons lightning during thunderstorms when your trident hits a mob.
Impaling does extra damage to mobs in water or rain.
Quick Charge makes crossbows load faster.
Density makes mace smash attacks hit even harder.
Breach lets mace hits ignore some of the target's armor.
Wind Burst launches you back up after a mace smash. Chain them!
Curse of Binding means you can't take that armor off. Read before wearing!
Curse of Vanishing makes the item disappear when you die.
Librarian villagers sell enchanted books. Find one with Mending!
You can reset a librarian's trades by breaking and replacing their lectern, as long as you haven't traded yet.
Villager prices drop if you cure them or defend their village.
Trading with villagers levels them up and unlocks better trades.
Lock in good trades by trading once. The villager keeps that offer.
Fletcher villagers buy sticks. Easy emeralds early on!
Farmer villagers buy crops for emeralds. Grow lots of wheat or carrots!
Cleric villagers buy rotten flesh and sell ender pearls!
Cartographer villagers sell explorer maps to monuments and mansions.
Armorer villagers sell diamond armor at higher levels.
Toolsmiths sell enchanted diamond tools at master level.
Masons sell pretty building blocks like glazed terracotta.
Shepherds sell beds and wool in every color.
Leatherworkers sell horse armor and leather goods.
Butchers buy raw meat. Easy money if you have an animal farm!
Weaponsmiths sell enchanted swords and axes.
Fishermen buy fish and sell campfires.
Villagers need a job block to get a profession. Place one near an unemployed villager!
Nitwits in green coats never take a job. They just vibe.
Protect your villagers from zombies with fences and light!
Villagers ring the bell and hide inside when raiders show up.
Wandering traders despawn after a while. Trade quickly if they have something good!
Kill the wandering trader's llamas and you get leads. A bit mean, though!
Iron golems spawn when villagers feel threatened. They make great iron farms.
Turtles drop scutes when babies grow up. Make turtle shells for water breathing!
Armadillo scutes make wolf armor. Brush the armadillo to get them!
Wolf armor protects your dog a lot. Repair it with more scutes!
Sit your pets down by right-clicking them so they don't follow you into danger.
Tamed wolves teleport to you if they get too far away, unless they're sitting.
Cats can sit on chests and stop them from opening. Peanut Butter does this on purpose.
Horses can wear armor. Find horse armor in chests or buy it from leatherworkers.
Feed horses golden apples or golden carrots to breed them.
Llamas can carry chests. Great for long trips!
Llamas follow a lead in caravans. Lead one and the others follow!
Donkeys and mules can carry chests too.
Camels can carry two players. Bring a friend!
Camels can dash forward. Great for jumping gaps!
Striders need a saddle and a warped fungus on a stick to ride.
Pigs need a saddle and a carrot on a stick. Slow but fun!
Happy ghasts can carry up to four players. Put a harness on them!
Bees follow you if you hold flowers. Lead them home!
Breed bees with flowers to grow your hive.
Glass bottles on a full beehive give honey bottles.
Shears on a full beehive give honeycomb. Use a campfire under it first!
Honey blocks slow you down and stop jumps. Great for parkour challenges!
Slime blocks bounce you up. Fall on them to avoid damage!
Hay bales reduce fall damage. Great for landing pads!
Powder snow catches your fall, but you'll freeze if you stay inside.
Scaffolding is easy to climb and easy to break. Perfect for building tall!
Ladders and vines let you climb walls. Sneak on them to stop moving.
Twisting vines and weeping vines can be climbed too.
Water elevators made with soul sand push you up fast!
Magma blocks under water make bubble columns that pull you down.
Doors placed underwater make air pockets you can breathe in.
Kelp grows fast underwater. Dry it in a furnace for a quick snack!
Dried kelp blocks are a great furnace fuel.
A bucket of lava smelts a hundred items in a furnace!
Coal blocks last much longer than coal in a furnace.
Bamboo is a weak but super fast fuel.
Use a stonecutter to make stairs and slabs with less waste.
Smoker for food, blast furnace for ores. Normal furnace for everything else!
Name your chests on an anvil and the name shows when you open them.
Crafters can craft automatically with redstone. Great for factories!
Comparators can read how full a chest is.
Observers send a signal when the block in front of them changes.
Repeaters can delay signals and extend them up to 15 blocks.
Redstone dust only carries power 15 blocks. Use repeaters for longer lines!
Daylight sensors can turn lights on at night automatically.
Pressure plates make hands-free doors. Watch out, mobs can trigger them too!
Tripwire hooks and string make great traps or alarms.
Pistons can push up to twelve blocks.
Sticky pistons pull blocks back. Great for hidden doors!
Obsidian and bedrock can't be pushed by pistons.
Hoppers can pull items from chests above them.
Droppers spit items out, dispensers use them. Dispensers can place water or shoot arrows!
Dispensers can put armor on players and saddles on pigs.
Note blocks change pitch when you click them. Make music!
Copper bulbs toggle on and off with each redstone pulse.
Target blocks are great for archery games with redstone.
Lightning rods protect your wooden house from fires during storms.
Lightning rods also give a redstone signal when struck.
Sculk sensors detect vibrations. Use them in redstone builds!
Calibrated sculk sensors only listen to certain vibrations.
A lever is the simplest on-off switch.
Buttons give a short pulse. Wood buttons can be pressed by arrows too!
Rails need a pickaxe to break fast. Powered rails need gold!
Powered rails need redstone power to boost carts.
Detector rails send a signal when a minecart passes over them.
Activator rails can drop players out of minecarts.
Minecarts with hoppers can collect items as they roll.
Minecarts with chests move lots of items at once.
Boats with chests carry items across water!
Elytra need repairing often. Mending is a must!
Fireworks with stars damage you when used with elytra. Use plain rockets!
Firework rockets with more gunpowder fly farther.
Look down slightly when gliding to keep your speed.
Don't fly elytra into walls. It hurts a lot!
Slow falling is a great backup when your elytra breaks mid-air.
Riptide tridents can launch you into the air for elytra takeoffs in the rain.
Wind charges can boost your elytra takeoff too!
Always carry a spare pair of elytra on long trips. Or Mending!
Spyglasses let you scout far away. Great for finding structures!
Explorer maps from cartographers lead to ocean monuments and woodland mansions.
Buried treasure maps come from shipwrecks. The X marks the spot!
Buried treasure is usually right at the center of the chunk. Dig at the X!
Heart of the sea comes from buried treasure. You need it for a conduit!
Conduits need prismarine blocks around them to activate.
Night vision potions make underwater exploring much easier.
Water breathing potions are made with pufferfish.
Turtle Master potions make you very slow but very tough.
Potions of strength are made with blaze powder.
Potions of swiftness use sugar.
Potions of healing use glistering melon slices.
Potions of regeneration use ghast tears.
Potions of night vision use golden carrots.
Fermented spider eyes turn many potions into their opposite.
Redstone dust makes potions last longer.
Glowstone dust makes potions stronger, but shorter.
Gunpowder turns potions into splash potions.
Dragon's breath turns splash potions into lingering potions.
Awkward potions are made with nether wart. They're the base for most potions!
Blaze powder fuels brewing stands. Keep some handy!
Weakness potions don't need nether wart. Just a fermented spider eye in water!
Slow falling potions use phantom membranes.
Invisibility potions hide you, but your armor still shows!
Brew potions in batches of three to save ingredients.
Throw a splash potion of healing at your feet in a pinch!
Splash potions of harming heal undead mobs instead of hurting them.
Healing potions hurt zombies and skeletons. Splash them!
Witches drink potions to heal. Hit them fast!
Witch huts in swamps are great for witch farms.
Strongholds have libraries and the end portal. Bring eyes of ender!
You need twelve eyes of ender to fill an end portal frame, but some may already be there.
Eyes of ender sometimes break when you throw them. Bring extras!
Blaze rods make blaze powder. Blaze powder plus ender pearls makes eyes of ender.
Ender pearls come from Endermen, or from trading with clerics and piglins.
Beat the dragon, then throw an ender pearl into the gateway to reach outer islands.
End cities are tall towers. Bring blocks to climb, and slow falling!
Look for end ships near end cities. They have the elytra!
Purple shulker shells make shulker boxes. Kill shulkers in end cities to get them.
Shulker boxes keep items inside when broken. You can even dye them!
Chorus fruit can be popped in a furnace to make popped chorus fruit for purpur blocks.
The dragon egg can be collected with a piston or by making it fall onto a torch.
Respawn the dragon with four end crystals on the exit portal.
Don't place beds in the End. They explode!
Endermen in the End can be farmed for ender pearls and experience.
Before fighting the Wither, bring milk for wither effect and lots of healing.
Fight the Wither underground so it can't fly away and break everything.
The Wither is weak to Smite. It's undead!
When the Wither drops below half health, arrows stop working. Switch to melee!
Beacons give powerful effects like Haste and Speed. Build one with a nether star!
A full beacon pyramid unlocks the second power slot.
Haste II from a beacon makes mining super fast.
Recovery compasses point to where you last died. Crafted with echo shards!
Echo shards come from ancient city chests.
Ancient cities have enchanted golden apples sometimes. Lucky!
Every sculk shrieker scream brings the Warden closer. Don't set them off again and again!
If the Warden appears, leave. It's not meant to be fought!
Wool and carpet hide your footsteps from sculk sensors.
Sneaking doesn't make vibrations. Sneak in the deep dark!
Trial chambers have lots of loot. Bring food and good armor!
Trial spawners give keys when you beat them.
Drink an ominous bottle before a trial chamber for harder fights and better loot!
Ominous bottles come from raid captains now.
Breezes shoot wind charges that knock you around. Stay away from edges!
Collect breeze rods to craft wind charges.
Copper doors and trapdoors are found in trial chambers. Waxed copper stays shiny!
Trial chambers have decorated pots. Break them for loot!
Vaults only give you loot once per player. Bring friends for more!
Archaeology needs a brush. Craft it with a feather, copper and a stick.
Trail ruins are buried. Look for gravel and terracotta peeking out!
Suspicious gravel and sand break if you mine them. Brush gently!
Pottery sherds make decorated pots with pictures.
Sniffer eggs come from brushing suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins.
Sniffer eggs hatch faster on moss blocks.
Sniffers dig up torchflower seeds and pitcher pods.
Armor trims come from structures all over the world. Collect them all!
The Silence armor trim is the rarest. It's in ancient cities!
Netherite upgrade templates come from bastion remnants.
Smithing templates are used up when you use them. Copy them first!
Ancient debris is most common around Y 15 in the Nether.
Mining ancient debris needs a diamond or netherite pickaxe.
Four netherite scraps and four gold ingots make one netherite ingot.
Netherite gear gives knockback resistance too.
Netherite items float in lava instead of burning. Pick them up quickly!
Bastions have piglin brutes. They don't care about gold armor!
Gilded blackstone in bastions sometimes drops gold nuggets.
Piglins can give you ender pearls, fire resistance potions and more through bartering.
Baby piglins don't barter. They just play.
Zombified piglins drop gold nuggets. Great for gold farms!
Nether fortresses are made of nether bricks. Look for long bridges!
Blaze spawners in fortresses give blaze rods. Bring snowballs or fire resistance!
Nether wart grows on soul sand. Find it in fortresses!
Basalt deltas are tricky. Bring lots of blocks and careful steps.
Warped forests are the safest Nether biome. Endermen live there, though!
Crimson forests have hoglins and piglins. Be careful!
Soul sand valleys have ghasts and skeletons. Lots of open space!
Nether wastes are the classic Nether. Lava, netherrack and ghasts!
Glowstone grows on the Nether ceiling. Silk Touch keeps the block whole.
Shroomlights are found in huge fungi. They make great lights!
Crying obsidian drips purple tears. It's needed for respawn anchors.
Nether portals need at least ten obsidian. The corners are optional!
You can light a nether portal with flint and steel or a fire charge.
Ghast fireballs can't break cobblestone. Wrap your Nether portal in it!
Link portals by building them at matching coordinates. Divide Overworld coordinates by eight!
The Nether roof is above bedrock. Getting there is tricky and risky!
Lava in the Nether flows faster and farther. Extra careful!
Water evaporates in the Nether. You can't place it.
Use a fire resistance potion before mining in the Nether.
Mark your Nether portal with a tall pillar. Easy to spot!
Magma cream comes from magma cubes. Great for fire resistance potions!
Wither skeleton skulls drop rarely. Looting III helps a lot!
Wither roses hurt you. Don't walk through them!
Strongholds can also be found by following eyes of ender. They fly toward it!
Eyes of ender sink into the ground right above a stronghold.
Silverfish hide in stronghold walls. Don't break stone bricks carelessly!
Stronghold libraries have enchanted books and lots of bookshelves.
Desert temples have a hidden room with TNT. Don't step on the pressure plate!
Dig down from the side in desert temples to avoid the trap.
Jungle temples have arrow traps and puzzles. Watch for tripwires!
Igloos sometimes hide a basement with a zombie villager and a brewing stand.
Woodland mansions have illagers and secret rooms.
Ocean monuments have gold blocks and sponges inside.
Elder guardians give Mining Fatigue. Bring milk!
Guardians shoot lasers. Break line of sight to stop them!
Shipwrecks have loot chests and sometimes treasure maps.
Ocean ruins have suspicious sand and loot chests.
Pillager outposts have an allay prison sometimes. Free them!
Pillager captains carry banners. Their banner is called the ominous banner.
Mineshafts have cave spider spawners. Bring torches and break the spawner!
Mineshafts have chest minecarts with loot.
Dungeons have spawners and chests. Great for early loot!
Light up a spawner with torches to stop it from spawning mobs.
Geodes have amethyst. Use Silk Touch for budding amethyst? Nope, it can't be moved!
Amethyst clusters only grow on budding amethyst blocks.
Ruined portals have loot chests with gold items.
Villages can have loot chests in the blacksmith's house.
Trail ruins are great for archaeology and armor trims!
Ancient cities are deep in the deep dark, below Y 0.
Lush caves have axolotls, glow berries and moss.
Dripstone caves have pointed dripstone that hurts if you fall on it.
Pointed dripstone can drip water or lava into cauldrons!
Big caves are great for finding ores, but light them up!
Spelunk with a water bucket and a stack of blocks.
Look at walls in big caves for exposed diamonds.
Diamonds are most common deep down, around Y -58.
Redstone ore is common near the bottom of the world.
Gold is extra common in badlands biomes.
Copper ore drops lots of raw copper. Fortune makes it even better!
Raw ore blocks save space. Craft nine raw iron into a block!
Deepslate ores take longer to mine. Efficiency helps!
Tuff, calcite and smooth basalt are nice building blocks from caves.
Moss spreads with bone meal. Great for decoration!
Azalea bushes grow into trees above lush caves.
Rooted dirt above caves can mean a lush cave below!
Spore blossoms hang in lush caves. They're so pretty!
Glow lichen grows on cave walls. Shears collect it!
Use shears on leaves to collect them. They make great decorations!
Saplings come from leaves. Plant them to grow more trees!
Big oak trees can grow from saplings. Plant four dark oak or spruce in a square for giant trees!
Jungle trees can grow huge if you plant four saplings in a square.
Mangrove propagules grow on mangrove leaves.
Cherry saplings make pink trees. My favorite!
Pale oak saplings grow in pale gardens. Plant them in a square of four!
Bamboo grows super fast. Great for scaffolding!
Cactus can hurt mobs. Use it in mob traps!
Sugar cane makes paper and sugar. Both super useful!
Paper is used for books, maps and fireworks.
Books need paper and leather. Kill cows for leather!
Bookshelves are made with books and planks. Great for libraries!
Chiseled bookshelves can hold books and work with comparators!
Lecterns let you share books with other players.
Write a book with a book and quill. Sign it to make it final!
Maps can be expanded at a cartography table.
Banners on maps make markers. Use a banner on a map to mark a spot!
Item frames with maps make wall maps.
Glow item frames light up what's inside them.
Armor stands display your armor. Great for decorating!
Paintings come in random sizes based on the space you place them in.
Flower pots hold flowers, saplings and even small cacti.
Candles can be lit and placed in groups of four.
Candles on cakes make a birthday cake!
Campfires cook food slowly without fuel.
Soul campfires keep piglins away.
Campfires can be put out with a shovel or water.
Signs can now be edited after you place them. Just click them!
Honeycomb on signs waxes them so nobody can edit them.
Dyes can color signs, glass, wool, terracotta, concrete and more.
Concrete powder turns into concrete when it touches water.
Terracotta comes from smelting clay blocks.
Glazed terracotta has patterns. Smelt dyed terracotta to get it!
Glazed terracotta can't be pulled by sticky pistons. Neat for redstone!
Glass is made by smelting sand. Tinted glass blocks light!
Stained glass beams change the color of beacon beams!
Mob heads can be worn. A creeper head lowers how close creepers notice you!
Wear a skeleton skull and skeletons notice you from less far away!
