Cows give milk when you use a bucket on them, and milk removes all potion effects.
Mooshrooms only live in mushroom fields.
Shearing a mooshroom gives you mushrooms, and the mooshroom turns into a normal cow.
You can dye sheep in all sixteen colors.
Chickens can be bred with any kind of seeds.
Rabbits can be bred with carrots, golden carrots or dandelions.
Rabbits sneak into farms and eat the carrots.
A rabbit's foot is used to brew potions of Leaping.
A full beehive can be harvested with shears for honeycomb or with a glass bottle for honey.
A bee sting poisons you on Normal and Hard difficulty.
Foxes can be bred with sweet berries or glow berries.
Foxes pounce on chickens, rabbits, fish and baby turtles.
Pandas only live in jungles and bamboo jungles.
Playful pandas roll over and tumble around.
Worried pandas hide their faces during thunderstorms.
Aggressive pandas hit back when you hit them.
Up to two parrots can ride on your shoulders, one on each side.
Parrots come in five colors: red, blue, green, cyan and gray.
Polar bears live in snowy and icy biomes.
Bats sleep hanging upside down from the ceiling.
Bats only spawn in the dark, below sea level.
Baby striders sometimes ride on an adult strider's back.
Hoglins drop porkchops and leather.
Zoglins are zombified hoglins that attack almost everything around them.
Adult piglins hunt baby hoglins.
Piglin brutes guard bastions. They don't care about gold and always attack.
Piglins pick up gold items they find and admire them for a while.
Piglins celebrate after they defeat a hoglin.
Baby piglins never grow up.
The wandering trader drinks a potion of Invisibility at night and milk in the morning.
The wandering trader leaves after a while, so trade quickly.
Villagers wear different clothes depending on the biome they're from.
There are thirteen villager professions, from armorer to weaponsmith.
Villagers level up from Novice to Master, and their badge changes as they do.
Farmer villagers plant and harvest crops all by themselves.
Villagers share bread with each other by throwing it.
Villagers breed when they have enough food and there are free beds nearby.
A librarian's trades change until you trade with them once. Then they're locked.
Cartographers sell explorer maps to ocean monuments, woodland mansions and trial chambers.
Clerics sell redstone, lapis lazuli, glowstone and ender pearls.
Diamond ore gives more diamonds with Fortune, up to four from a single block with Fortune III.
Mining ancient debris needs a diamond or netherite pickaxe, and Fortune doesn't help.
Four netherite scraps and four gold ingots make one netherite ingot.
Smelting ancient debris gives netherite scrap, one per block.
Emerald ore only generates in mountain biomes.
Lapis lazuli is used for enchanting, and one ore can drop up to nine pieces.
Redstone ore lights up when you touch it or walk on it.
Coal is the most common ore, and you can find it high up in mountains.
Copper ore drops raw copper, and Fortune gives you even more.
Iron ore is most common in two places: deep underground and high in the mountains.
Gold ore in the Nether drops gold nuggets instead of raw gold.
Deepslate ores look darker and take longer to mine than normal ores.
Nether quartz ore gives experience when you mine it.
Raw ore blocks let you store nine raw ores in one block.
Glass is made by smelting sand, and tinted glass blocks all light.
Smooth stone is made by smelting stone twice: first cobblestone into stone, then stone into smooth stone.
Terracotta is made by smelting clay blocks, and glazed terracotta by smelting dyed terracotta.
Glazed terracotta can't be moved by slime blocks or honey blocks, but pistons can push it.
Concrete powder turns into concrete when it touches water.
There are sixteen colors of wool, concrete, terracotta, glazed terracotta, stained glass, candles, beds and banners.
Candles can be placed up to four on one block, and lit with flint and steel.
You can put a candle on a cake. Only one, sadly.
Lanterns can hang from the ceiling or stand on the ground.
Soul torches, soul lanterns and soul campfires burn blue and keep piglins away.
Campfires cook food without fuel and send smoke up high, even higher with a hay bale under them.
Sea pickles glow brighter the more of them you put on one block, up to four.
Coral dies and turns gray when it's not touching water.
Kelp grows tall in the ocean, and dried kelp blocks are a great furnace fuel.
Lily pads can be walked on, and boats break them.
Vines grow down slowly, and you can climb them like ladders.
Glow berries grow on cave vines and light up the caves.
Spore blossoms drop green particles and only grow on ceilings in lush caves.
Big dripleaf tilts down when you stand on it, so don't stay too long.
Azalea trees grow above lush caves, so a flowering azalea is a hint to dig down.
Pink petals can be stacked up to four on one block.
Torchflowers were once extinct, until sniffers dug up their seeds.
Pitcher plants are two blocks tall and also come from ancient seeds sniffers find.
Wither roses give the Wither effect and grow where the Wither defeats a mob.
Sunflowers always face east.
Melon and pumpkin stems need an empty block next to them to grow fruit.
Wheat, carrots, potatoes and beetroots all grow on farmland.
Mushrooms grow in the dark, on almost any block.
Chorus flowers can be planted on end stone to grow new chorus plants.
Leaves decay when they're not near a log, and sometimes drop saplings, sticks or apples.
Only oak and dark oak leaves drop apples.
Jungle and spruce saplings grow into giant trees when planted in a square of four.
Mangrove trees grow propagules that hang from their leaves.
Cherry trees grow in cherry groves, and their logs have a pink inside.
Pale oak trees grow in the pale garden, together with pale moss and pale hanging moss.
Bamboo can be crafted into bamboo planks and bamboo mosaic.
Scaffolding is made from bamboo and string.
Sponges are found in ocean monuments and dropped by elder guardians.
A single sponge can soak up a lot of water around it at once.
Slime blocks are used in flying machines because they pull blocks along when pushed.
Pistons can push up to twelve blocks at once.
Obsidian and bedrock can't be pushed by pistons.
Sticky pistons pull the block back when they retract.
Redstone dust carries a signal up to fifteen blocks before it needs a repeater.
Redstone repeaters can delay a signal by up to four ticks.
Redstone comparators can read how full a chest, hopper or cauldron is.
Lightning rods give off a redstone signal when lightning strikes them.
Sculk sensors can detect sounds through walls and turn them into redstone signals.
Note blocks can play many instruments: a harp, bass, drums, bells, flutes, chimes, xylophones and more.
A note block with a mob head on top plays that mob's sound.
Tripwire hooks with string make a tripwire that sends a redstone signal when walked through.
Pressure plates come in wood, stone and two weighted kinds made of gold and iron.
Dispensers shoot arrows, place water and lava, equip armor and use many items.
Droppers just drop items, while dispensers use them.
Hoppers pull items from chests above them and push them into containers below.
A hopper can be locked with a redstone signal.
Daylight detectors give a stronger signal the brighter the sun is.
Rails can be powered with powered rails, which need gold to craft.
Detector rails send a redstone signal when a minecart rolls over them.
Activator rails can make TNT minecarts explode and kick out passengers.
Minecarts with furnaces can push other minecarts.
Minecarts can carry mobs, so they're great for moving villagers.
A boat can carry two players, or a player and a mob.
Boats with chests can carry items instead of a second passenger.
Rafts are bamboo boats, and they float just like wooden boats.
Ladders let you climb walls, and holding sneak makes you stop on them.
Doors can be opened by hand, but iron doors need redstone.
Trapdoors can be used to crawl through one-block gaps.
Signs can be dyed, made glowing with a glow ink sac and waxed so nobody can edit them.
Hanging signs hang from chains below blocks.
Item frames show items on walls, and glow item frames are always bright.
Armor stands can wear armor and hold items, and you can give them arms with commands.
Paintings come in many sizes, and the one you get depends on how much space there is.
A banner on a shield shows its pattern on the shield.
Bookshelves can be crafted from planks and books, and chiseled bookshelves store up to six books.
Jukeboxes can play music discs, and allays dance to them.
Beacons give effects like Speed, Haste, Resistance, Jump Boost, Strength and Regeneration.
A beacon needs a nether star to be crafted.
Conduits give you Conduit Power underwater: you breathe, see clearly and mine faster.
Respawn anchors can hold up to four charges of glowstone.
Lodestones are crafted from chiseled stone bricks and a netherite ingot.
Ender chests are crafted from obsidian and an eye of ender.
Enchanting tables are crafted from a book, diamonds and obsidian.
Anvils need three blocks of iron and four iron ingots.
Grindstones can repair two damaged tools of the same kind into one.
Looms make banner patterns easy.
Smokers cook food twice as fast as a normal furnace.
Furnaces give you experience for smelting things.
A lava bucket burns for 100 items in a furnace, the longest of any fuel.
A block of coal smelts 80 items.
Wooden tools and planks can be used as furnace fuel.
Sharpness, Smite and Bane of Arthropods can't be on the same sword.
Smite does extra damage to undead mobs like zombies, skeletons and the Wither.
Bane of Arthropods does extra damage to spiders, bees, silverfish and endermites, and slows them down.
Looting makes mobs drop more loot, up to level III.
Fire Aspect sets mobs on fire, so cows drop cooked steak.
Knockback pushes mobs further away when you hit them.
Sweeping Edge makes your sword's sweep attack stronger in Java Edition.
Unbreaking makes your tools last longer, up to level III.
Efficiency makes tools mine faster, up to level V.
Fortune gives more drops from ores, crops and some other blocks.
Silk Touch lets you pick up blocks as they are, like glass, ice and grass blocks.
Power makes bows hit harder, up to level V.
Punch knocks mobs back when your arrows hit them.
Flame sets arrows on fire, and they can light TNT.
Infinity lets you shoot forever with just one arrow in your inventory.
Multishot makes a crossbow shoot three arrows at once.
Piercing lets crossbow arrows go through several mobs.
Quick Charge makes crossbows load faster.
Multishot and Piercing can't be on the same crossbow.
Respiration lets you breathe longer underwater.
Aqua Affinity makes you mine at normal speed underwater.
Depth Strider makes you walk faster underwater.
Blast Protection, Fire Protection, Projectile Protection and Protection can't be on the same armor piece.
Lure makes fish bite faster.
Density, Breach and Wind Burst are enchantments only for the mace.
Wind Burst launches you back up into the air after a mace hit.
Breach makes the mace go through armor.
Density makes the mace hit even harder for every block you fall.
Treasure enchantments like Mending and Frost Walker can't come from an enchanting table.
Enchanting costs lapis lazuli and experience levels.
Combining two items with the same enchantment level in an anvil can raise the level by one.
Name tags need an anvil to be renamed before you can use them.
Potions start with a water bottle and nether wart, which makes an awkward potion.
Redstone makes potions last longer, glowstone makes them stronger.
Gunpowder turns a potion into a splash potion.
Sugar brews potions of Swiftness.
A magma cream brews Fire Resistance.
A pufferfish brews Water Breathing.
A golden carrot brews Night Vision.
A ghast tear brews Regeneration.
Blaze powder brews Strength.
A glistering melon slice brews Healing.
A turtle shell brews the potion of the Turtle Master, which makes you slow but very tough.
A phantom membrane brews Slow Falling.
A spider eye brews Poison.
A fermented spider eye turns Night Vision into Invisibility.
A breeze rod brews the potion of Wind Charging.
Slime blocks brew Oozing, stone brews Infestation and cobwebs brew Weaving.
Tipped arrows are made by putting a lingering potion around arrows in a crafting table.
Potions of Healing hurt undead mobs, and potions of Harming heal them.
Wearing armor while invisible makes it easier for mobs to notice you.
Golden apples give Absorption and Regeneration.
Enchanted golden apples also give Resistance and Fire Resistance.
Chorus fruit can teleport you out of trouble, but you never know where.
Dried kelp is quick to eat, even if it doesn't fill much hunger.
Eating a rotten flesh can give you Hunger.
Raw chicken can give you food poisoning, so cook it first.
Spider eyes are food too, but they poison you.
Suspicious stew made with a lily of the valley gives Poison. Choose your flowers carefully!
Cake can be eaten in seven slices, and you can share it with friends.
Pumpkin pie is crafted from a pumpkin, sugar and an egg.
Cookies are crafted from wheat and cocoa beans.
Beetroot soup is made from six beetroots and a bowl.
Rabbit stew is one of the most filling foods in the game.
Glow berries can be eaten, and you can also feed them to foxes.
Sweet berries can be eaten, but they don't fill you up much.
Sprinting, jumping and fighting make you hungry faster.
When your hunger bar is full, your health regenerates quickly.
On Peaceful difficulty, your hunger never goes down.
Experience orbs come from mobs, mining some ores, smelting, breeding and fishing.
The higher your level, the more experience you need for the next one.
When you die, you drop some of your experience, not all of it.
Bottles o' enchanting are sold by cleric villagers and found in some chests.
Hostile mobs can't spawn on bottom slabs, glass or leaves.
Mobs don't spawn within 24 blocks of a player.
Mobs far from any player despawn after a while, unless they're named or tamed.
A day in Minecraft is 24,000 ticks, and a tick is a twentieth of a second.
You can only sleep at night or during a thunderstorm.
Sleeping skips the night and clears the weather.
Thunderstorms let hostile mobs spawn during the day, because it gets dark enough.
Lightning can set grass and trees on fire.
Lightning strikes the highest point nearby, or a lightning rod if there is one.
Fire spreads to wood, wool, leaves and other burnable blocks.
Fire goes out faster in the rain.
Water flows seven blocks on flat ground. Lava flows three in the Overworld, but seven in the Nether.
Two water source blocks next to each other make an infinite water source.
Lava isn't infinite in Java Edition, except for pointed dripstone filling cauldrons.
Fall damage starts after falling more than three blocks.
Landing in water cancels all fall damage, even from very high up.
Landing on hay bales, honey blocks, slime blocks, cobwebs or beds reduces fall damage.
You can swim faster by sprinting underwater.
Drowning starts after about fifteen seconds underwater.
Dolphins, conduits and turtle shell helmets all help you breathe or swim underwater.
Players crawl when they're squeezed into a one-block-high space.
Elytra need a few blocks of height to start gliding.
Elytra take damage while you glide, one point every second.
Firework rockets boost you while flying with elytra.
Flying into a wall with elytra hurts, so be careful with speed.
The void below the world hurts you until you die.
At the edge of the world, the terrain used to turn into the Far Lands. They were removed in Beta 1.8.
Minecraft worlds are made of chunks, each sixteen by sixteen blocks wide.
Spawn chunks were removed in 1.21.9. Before that, chunks around world spawn stayed loaded.
A world seed decides how the whole world generates.
The same seed makes the same world on Java Edition, so you can share seeds with friends.
Torches give light level 14, lanterns and glowstone give 15.
Lightning changes some mobs: creepers get charged, pigs turn into zombified piglins, villagers into witches and red mooshrooms into brown ones.
Wolf armor can be dyed any color.
Desert temples hide a TNT trap under the treasure room. Never step on the pressure plate!
Jungle temples have tripwire traps with arrows and hidden levers.
Igloos sometimes have a secret basement with a zombie villager and a brewing stand.
Witch huts stand on stilts in swamps, and a black cat lives in each one.
Pillager outposts are watchtowers where pillagers keep spawning.
Mineshafts are full of cave spider spawners and rails.
Monster rooms, also called dungeons, have a spawner and up to two chests.
An end portal room's frame comes with some eyes of ender already in it, sometimes.
Ocean ruins come in stone and sandstone, depending on the water temperature.
Shipwrecks can contain treasure maps, emeralds and suspicious stew.
Ruined portals can be found in the Overworld and the Nether, often with a chest full of gold.
Trail ruins hide pottery sherds, dyes and music disc Relic in suspicious gravel.
Desert wells hide suspicious sand with pottery sherds.
Ancient cities have a huge structure in the middle that looks like a giant portal frame.
Trial chambers have ominous vaults that need ominous trial keys.
Bastion remnants come in four kinds: bridges, hoglin stables, housing units and treasure rooms.
End cities float on the outer End islands and some of them have an end ship nearby.
Woodland mansions are huge and can have a room with a fake end portal.
Ocean monuments are guarded by guardians and elder guardians and hide gold blocks inside.
There are more than 60 biomes in the Overworld.
Mushroom fields are among the rarest biomes and usually sit far out in the ocean.
Deserts have no rain, just sand, cactus and dead bushes.
Badlands are made of colorful terracotta layers.
Swamps have lily pads, slimes at night and witch huts.
Mangrove swamps have mud, frogs and mangrove trees with huge roots.
Jungles are home to parrots, ocelots, pandas and jungle temples.
Snowy plains have igloos, polar bears and snowy villages.
Frozen oceans have icebergs and polar bears floating on ice.
Deep oceans are home to ocean monuments.
Lush caves have glow berries, moss, azaleas and axolotls.
Dripstone caves are full of stalactites and stalagmites.
The deep dark is covered in sculk and is home to the Warden and ancient cities.
Meadows are high, flowery fields where bees and beehives are common.
Stony peaks are mountain tops made of stone and calcite.
Birch forests are full of white birch trees, and old growth birch forests have extra-tall ones.
Dark forests are so dense that hostile mobs can spawn there during the day.
Sunflower plains are the only place where sunflowers grow naturally.
The Nether has five biomes: Nether wastes, crimson forests, warped forests, soul sand valleys and basalt deltas.
Soul sand valleys are home to skeletons, ghasts and endermen, and full of fossils.
Basalt deltas are full of magma cubes and ghasts.
Crimson forests are home to hoglins and piglins.
Endermen live in warped forests in big numbers.
The End is made of end stone and floats over the void.
The main End island has 10 obsidian pillars, each with an end crystal on top.
The outer End islands have chorus plants, end cities and end ships.
The Overworld has a sea level at Y 63.
The Nether has a lava sea at Y 31.
The Nether is 128 blocks tall and has a bedrock roof.
Building above the Nether roof is possible, but it's very empty up there.
Nether portals can be any size from 4 by 5 up to 23 by 23 blocks of obsidian.
A Nether portal can be lit with flint and steel, a fire charge, or anything that starts a fire.
Zombified piglins sometimes walk out of Nether portals in the Overworld.
Jens Bergensten, known as Jeb, took over as lead developer in 2011.
Minecraft 1.0 was released at MineCon in November 2011.
Minecraft was originally inspired by games like Infiniminer and Dwarf Fortress.
The Nether was added in Alpha in 2010, back then called the Halloween Update.
The Ender Dragon and the End were added in 2011, right before Minecraft 1.0.
The Update Aquatic in 2018 added dolphins, turtles, tridents and coral reefs.
The Nether Update in 2020 added netherite, piglins, striders and new Nether biomes.
The Caves and Cliffs update was so big that it came out in two parts, in 2021.
The Wild Update in 2022 added the deep dark, frogs, allays and mangrove swamps.
Trails and Tales in 2023 added cherry groves, sniffers, camels and archaeology.
Minecraft has a Minecraft Live show where Mojang shows what's coming next.
The mob vote was a yearly vote where players picked a new mob. It ended after 2023.
Minecraft has sold over 300 million copies.
Minecraft Education is used in schools to teach things like coding, history and chemistry.
Minecraft has a spin-off called Minecraft Dungeons, an adventure game in the Minecraft style.
Minecraft Legends is a strategy game set in the Minecraft world.
The game's splash texts are the little yellow messages on the title screen. There are hundreds of them.
The Minecraft title screen's panorama changes with many major updates.
Chickens were added to the game in 2010, and they've been laying eggs ever since.
Steve and Alex have been joined by more default skins, like Sunny, Kai, Ari, Zuri, Makena, Noor and Efe.
The Minecraft font is pixelated, just like everything else in the game.
Minecraft's music changes depending on where you are, like the Nether or the underwater biomes.
Disc "11" sounds like someone running from something. Nobody knows exactly what.
"Otherside" and "Pigstep" were made by Lena Raine, and "Relic" by Aaron Cherof.
"Creator" was composed by Lena Raine for the Tricky Trials update.
Mojang's office is in Stockholm, Sweden.
The original Minecraft logo was made with stone textures.
Naming a mob "Dinnerbone" was added as a joke about one of the developers, Nathan Adams.
The moon in Minecraft is square, just like the sun.
There's a 1 in 10,000 chance that the title screen says "Minceraft".
Mojang often hides fun names in the game, like "jeb_" for sheep and "Toast" for rabbits.
The "Far Lands" were a glitchy area at the edge of old Minecraft worlds, millions of blocks away.

joke_about: Why did {name} bring a ladder to the Nether? Someone said the prices there were going up!
{name} has so many chests that the chests have their own storage room.
{name} once got lost on the way to bed. In their own house. Twice.
They say {name} can find diamonds blindfolded. The blindfold just makes the digging slower.
{name} tried to tame a creeper. It went... explosively well.
Why does {name} carry a stack of torches everywhere? Because {name} is a bright idea!
{name}'s favorite exercise? Running away from creepers. Very good cardio.
{name} doesn't sort chests. {name} just calls it "surprise storage".
{name} named every cow on the farm. Now saying goodbye to the steaks is very emotional.
When {name} says "I'll just mine for five minutes", the sun has already set twice.
{name}'s build plans are like elytra flights: very ambitious, and sometimes ending in a wall.
Why did the enderman pick up {name}'s dirt block? Even endermen want a piece of {name}'s legendary dirt house!
{name} is so nice, even the zombies ask for a hug before attacking.
{name} walked into a bar. It was an iron bar. It hurt.
Why is {name} never cold in the snow? All those cozy wool sweaters, obviously.
{name} has a map for every biome, a map for every map, and still asks for directions.
How does {name} greet a skeleton? "Hey, how's it going? You look a bit bony today!"
{name} once spent an hour building a perfect house, then remembered doors exist.
{name}'s inventory is 90% cobblestone and 10% hope.
Why did {name} plant a torch? To grow a lighthouse!
{name} can talk to villagers for hours. The villagers just say "hmm", but {name} says they're great listeners.
{name}'s redstone contraptions are mysterious. Even {name} doesn't know what they do. But they look amazing!
If {name} had a coin for every time they fell into a ravine, {name} could buy a ladder.
Why did {name} bring a bucket of milk to the party? To clear the bad vibes!
{name} is the only player I know who says "please" to the crafting table.
{name} tried to boat up a waterfall. Points for confidence!
Why did the chicken cross the road? To get away from {name}'s cooking.
{name}'s pets have better armor than most players.
{name} says the Nether is just "a warm vacation spot".
Why did {name} get a job at the bakery? Because {name} kneads the bread!
{name} once traded with a villager for so long that the villager retired.
Legend says {name} still hasn't found the last piece of the netherite set. The search continues!
{name} built a farm so big that the cows needed a map.
{name} doesn't fear the Warden. The Warden fears {name}'s singing.
Why does {name} love the deep dark? It's the only place quiet enough for a nap.
{name} brought a cake to the Ender Dragon fight. Priorities!
Why did the creeper apologize to {name}? It realized it had blown things out of proportion.
{name}'s favorite block is the one they're standing on. {name} is very loyal like that.
{name} always says "one more trade". The villagers have stopped believing it.
{name} is so good at building, even the sheep line up for an autograph.
Why did {name} put a bed in every room? Just in case a nap emergency happens.

Rumor has it {name} once beat the Ender Dragon with a stick. The dragon was laughing too hard to fight back.
Rumor has it {name} can tame anything. Even the moon, on a good night.
Rumor has it {name}'s cooking is so good, the zombies line up for dinner.
Rumor has it {name} has a secret room full of cake. We all hope it's true.
Rumor has it {name} once talked a creeper out of exploding. With kindness. And a lot of running.
Rumor has it {name}'s cat is actually in charge of the base.
Rumor has it {name} knows where every slime chunk is. {name} just won't tell.
Legend says that if you whisper "{name}" in a cave, a torch appears on the wall.
Legend says {name}'s first house is still standing. It's made of dirt. It's beautiful.
Legend says {name} once found a diamond on the surface and fainted from joy.
Legend says {name} has the oldest wolf on the server. The wolf is wiser than all of us.
Legend says {name} once crafted a cake in under three seconds.
A wild {name} appears! It uses "build another chest". It's super effective!
A wild {name} appears! It's carrying three stacks of torches and a dream.
Achievement unlocked for {name}: "Built a house without forgetting the door". Took a few tries!
Achievement unlocked for {name}: "Petted fifty cats in one day". Truly heroic.
Achievement unlocked for {name}: "Got lost in a village". Impressive!
Achievement unlocked for {name}: "Made a farm bigger than the house". Classic {name}.
{name} vs. gravel: 0 to 1. Gravel always wins.
{name} vs. the creeper: it's a tie. Both ran away screaming.
{name} vs. the Ender Dragon: {name} won, but the dragon got some great hits in. Mostly on the furniture.
{name} vs. the baby zombie: still undecided. Rematch on Thursday.
{name} vs. the villager trades: villager 3, {name} 0. But {name} got a nice stick.
Roses are red, creepers are green, {name} builds the coziest base you've ever seen.
Roses are red, lapis is blue, {name} has more chests than a whole village does too.
Roses are red, diamonds are rare, {name} found three today and is stuck in a chair.
Roses are red, the Nether is hot, {name} went in with a plan and then forgot.
Roses are red, the sky is blue, {name} built a bridge that goes nowhere, it's true.
Roses are red, the dragon is black, {name} went to the End and forgot the way back.
Roses are red, cookies are sweet, {name} trades with villagers and never gets a treat.
Roses are red, gravel will fall, {name} has a chest for each item of all.
Knock knock. Who's there? {name}. {name} who? {name} with another stack of cobblestone for you!
Knock knock. Who's there? {name}. {name} who? {name}, and I brought cake!
Knock knock. Who's there? {name}. {name} who? {name} who's lost again, can I come in?
Knock knock. Who's there? {name}. {name} who? {name}, here to organize your chests!
{name} walks into a village. The villagers say "hmm". {name} says "hmm" back. A friendship is born.
{name} walks into the Nether. The ghasts cry. {name} cries too. It's a moment.
{name} walks into a cave. The cave says "not again".
{name} walks into a trial chamber. The breeze says "wind you like to leave?" {name} stays.
How do you know {name} has been to your base? There's a new torch every two blocks.
How do you know {name} is mining nearby? You can hear the happy humming through the walls.
How do you know {name} is home? The chickens are clucking with joy.
How do you know {name} found diamonds? The whole server hears about it. Twice.
How do you find {name} on the server? Follow the trail of flowers and bread crumbs.
What's {name}'s favorite type of music? Anything with a jukebox and a cat dancing to it.
What's {name}'s favorite dessert? Whatever's in the emergency cake chest.
What's {name}'s favorite mob? All of them. Except the one that blew up the garden.
What's {name}'s favorite time of day? Snack time. Every time is snack time.
What's {name}'s favorite block? The next one {name} gets to place.
What does {name} call a creeper with good manners? A friend. A very rare friend.
What does {name} do on a rainy day? Build an indoor farm. And an indoor pool. And an indoor rain.
What does {name} keep in the ender chest? More ender chests, probably.
If {name} were a block, {name} would be a lantern: warm, bright and always where you need one.
If {name} were a mob, {name} would be an allay: always helpful and happy to bring you things.
If {name} were an item, {name} would be a cake: everyone's happy when it shows up.
If {name} were a biome, {name} would be a cherry grove: pretty, cozy and full of surprises.
If {name} were an enchantment, {name} would be Mending: always fixing things.
If {name} were a potion, {name} would be Regeneration: good company makes everyone feel better.
{name} is like a torch in a dark cave: a little wobbly, but always lighting things up.
{name} is like a golden apple: rare, sweet and great to have around.
{name} is like a hopper: always collecting things and passing them on to friends.
{name} is like a Nether portal: a bit purple, a bit mysterious, and always leading to adventure.
{name} is like a beacon: you can see {name} coming from far away, and everyone feels stronger.
{name} is like a jukebox: brings good vibes wherever {name} goes.
Did you hear? {name} built a house so big that the villagers think it's a village.
Did you hear? {name} named a goat "Gerald". Gerald screams a lot. Gerald is loved.
Did you hear? {name} tried to teach a parrot to say "hello". It learned to say "hiss".
Did you hear? {name} found a woodland mansion and moved in. The vindicators are adjusting.
Did you hear? {name} has started a club for people who fell into ravines. It has many members.

lines: First things first: punch a tree, make a wooden pickaxe and mine some stone!
Get some stone tools! They're way better than wood.
Start simple: wood, a crafting table, then stone tools!
Time for iron! Find some iron ore and smelt it in a furnace.
Look for iron in caves or on mountainsides, then smelt it!
Get a furnace going and smelt your first iron ingot!
Make an iron pickaxe! You'll need it for diamonds.
Upgrade to an iron pickaxe next!
Iron pickaxe time! Then you can mine diamonds and gold.
Go diamond hunting! Around Y -58 is a great spot.
You've got an iron pickaxe, so go find diamonds!
Diamonds next! Bring torches and a water bucket.
Build an enchanting table! You need diamonds, obsidian and a book.
Time to enchant your gear! Make an enchanting table.
Get an enchanting table and some bookshelves around it!
You haven't been to the Nether yet! Build a portal out of obsidian and light it.
Nether time! You need ten obsidian and flint and steel.
Ready for the Nether? Bring gold armor so piglins leave you alone!
Look for a Nether fortress! Dark brick walls in the distance.
Find a fortress in the Nether. Blazes live there!
Explore the Nether until you spot a fortress. Bring fire resistance!
Get some blaze rods from the blazes in the fortress!
Blaze rods next! You'll need them for brewing and eyes of ender.
Hunt some blazes. Snowballs work great against them!
Try brewing! Grab some nether wart for your first potions.
You have blaze rods, so make a brewing stand!
Brewing time! Fire resistance is a great first potion.
Craft some eyes of ender and find a stronghold!
Throw an eye of ender and follow it to a stronghold!
Get ender pearls, mix them with blaze powder, and track down the stronghold!
Fill the End portal and step in. If you dare!
You found the stronghold! Now fill the portal with eyes of ender.
The End is waiting! Bring lots of blocks and a bow.
Defeat the Ender Dragon! Destroy the end crystals first.
Dragon time! Bring a bow, blocks and slow falling potions.
Take down the Ender Dragon. Don't look the Endermen in the eye!
Throw an ender pearl into the End gateway and visit the outer islands!
The outer End islands are waiting. Use the gateway!
Explore beyond the dragon's island. There are End cities out there!
Find an End city with a ship and grab the elytra!
Look for End ships. One of them has wings for you!
Elytra hunt! End cities with ships have them.
Mine for ancient debris around Y 15 in the Nether!
Go find ancient debris. Beds explode in the Nether… useful!
Ancient debris hunt! It's the way to netherite.
Collect enough netherite for a full set of armor!
Upgrade all your armor to netherite. You'll need templates from bastions.
Full netherite armor is the goal! Look in bastions for upgrade templates.
Ready for a challenge? Summon the Wither!
Collect three wither skeleton skulls and fight the Wither.
The Wither is waiting. Build a safe arena first!
Use your nether star to make a beacon!
Beacon time! You'll need a pyramid of iron, gold or diamond blocks.
Build a beacon and pick a cool power!
Make your beacon pyramid full size! Four layers for all the powers.
Upgrade your beacon to full power!
Go for a full beacon. Lots of mining ahead!
Trade with a villager! Emeralds open up so much.
Find a village and start trading!
Villagers have great stuff. Go trade with one!
Find a trial chamber! They're full of loot and breezes.
Trial chambers are underground. Go find one!
Explore a trial chamber and grab some trial keys!
Sneak into an ancient city! Very quietly.
Go find an ancient city in the deep dark. Don't wake the Warden!
Ancient city time. Swift Sneak leggings are hidden there!
Visit every Nether biome! Have you seen a warped forest yet?
Explore all of the Nether. There are five biomes to see!
Go on a Nether tour: crimson, warped, basalt, soul sand and wastes!
With your elytra, visit every biome for Adventuring Time!
Fly around the world and collect all the biomes!
You can fly now, so go see every biome!

keyword_intents._comment: Small talk in any wording: a message matches when it contains one of the triggers and every other word is filler or one of the intent's words. A single real content word sends it to the wiki search instead. strip_start/strip_end are removed before matching ("can you tell me a joke please").

triggers: what are you up to today
what are you up to right now
not what i was looking for

feelings._comment: After Merl asks how someone is (ask_feeling, or after how_are_you), their next message is matched against these phrases (the longest match wins, so "not bad" beats "bad"; ties go by order) and gets a feeling_<name> line. ask_back phrases ("good, you?") add an about_me line.

stat_milestones._comment: In-game statistic milestones Merl celebrates (stat_<name> pools). distance is in kilometers, hours in hours played.
